title: Production Planning Manager
jd_text: POSITION OVERVIEW: The role of the Production Planning Manager is to work hands on with the Product Manufacturing, Planning , Scheduling, Procurement, Project Management, Engineering and Configuration Control teams to develop and implement a Production Planning strategy. KEY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES: Accomplishing department objectives by managing staff of Production Planners including recruiting, selecting, orientating and training employees as well as managing their schedules and performance to assigned tasks Serving as a core team member to drive optimization of the MRP/ERP system Working closely with Production, Engineering, Purchasing and Master Scheduler as needed to ensure accurate material planning Assist with tracking material movement throughout the shops Work closely with production leads/supervisors to insure they have what is needed to complete their jobs. Completing deliverables of the Production Planners as needed to cover peak workloads and/or absences Any other duties as assigned by TAS JOB SKILLS : Strong knowledge of ERP/MRP systems Strong written and oral communication skills across all levels of an organization Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings. Knowledge of manufacturing and supply chain principles Proven ability to meet deadlines and to multi-task on multiple projects Possess excellent inter-personal skills and the ability to work effectively in a team environment Coaching, training and motivational skills; ability to lead a team EDUCATION & TRAINING : Bachelor of Science or technical degree from an accredited university Extensive industry or military experience may be considered in lieu of a degree MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: 5 -7 years production planning experience in an engineer to order environment 3-5 years management experience with at least 3-5 direct reports MRP key user experience Ability to quickly grasp new technologies while adapting to frequent changes in assignment and business direction Solid foundational knowledge of engineering and fabrication processes PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS: Previous experience with Infor LN PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS/WORK ENVIRONMENT: Position is at least 75 % to 9 0 % at a desk working with computer. Ability to exert up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or a negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects, including the human body. Performs other physical activities including use of fingers, sitting, stooping, bending, crouching, talking, hearing and performing repetitive motions. Visual acuity requirements include color, depth perception and field of vision necessary to prepare and analyze data and figures, operate a computer terminal and conduct extensive reading. The incumbent will be subject to inside environmental conditions. COMPANY OVERVIEW: Join a team driven to excel in all that we do! When you join TAS, you join a Houston-headquartered company that is part of a large Houston-headquartered publicly traded company, Comfort Systems USA, with a solid reputation built on outstanding value, integrity, and customer focus. We offer our customers and employees the best of both worlds : a small company feel with the resources, talent, process, and international reach of a large company. TAS delivers innovative packaged modular systems that are engineered and manufactured in one of our Houston, TX facilities and utilized in data centers, power, and commercial/industrial utility system applications. TAS has successfully delivered and commissioned over 520 packages to over 33 countries. The company is headquartered in Houston, TX and has five ISO 9001 certified manufacturing facilities in Houston, encompassing 1.2m sq. feet with proximity to major shipping ports and interstate highways. TAS manages all logistics and transportation facilitating accelerated construction at customer’s facilities. TAS’ fastest growing business is the data center market. By applying deep expertise in cooling, thermodynamics, and power, TAS has developed an entire product line that revolutionizes data center delivery. With our tremendous market potential, advanced technological systems, entrepreneurial culture as well as a talented and productive workforce, we continue to set and exceed aggressive market penetration and financial goals. More information is available on the company website at: www.tas.com . IMPORTANT NOTICE: TAS has a tobacco-free workplace policy, under which individuals are not allowed to smoke or use tobacco or nicotine products on the TAS premises, while conducting TAS business off premises or take "smoking" breaks during working hours. “smoking” and “tobacco or nicotine products” includes, but is not limited to, product such as cigarettes, e-cigarettes, cigars, pipes, vaping, all forms of smokeless tobacco (chewing tobacco, snuff, dip) and clove cigarettes The above declarations are not intended to be an all-inclusive list of the duties and responsibilities of the job described, nor are they intended to be such a listing of the skills and abilities required to do the job. title: Senior Operations Manager
jd_text: About Us We are a global climate technologies company engineered for sustainability. We create sustainable and efficient residential, commercial and industrial spaces through HVACR technologies. We protect temperature-sensitive goods throughout the cold chain. And we bring comfort to people globally. Best-in-class engineering, design and manufacturing combined with category-leading brands in compression, controls, software and monitoring solutions result in next-generation climate technology that is built for the needs of the world ahead. Whether you are a professional looking for a career change, an undergraduate student exploring your first opportunity, or recent graduate with an advanced degree, we have opportunities that will allow you to innovate, be challenged and make an impact. Join our team and start your journey today! Description If you are a senior operations leader passionate about building high-performing teams and driving operational excellence, we have an exciting opportunity for you! Based at our Forney Distribution Center, you will be responsible for overseeing day-to-day warehouse operations, including inbound receiving, outbound shipping, inventory execution, and order fulfillment. This role is accountable for delivering safe, efficient, and reliable operations while driving continuous improvement across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity. You will partner closely with Customer Service, Inventory, Materials, Transportation, and other cross-functional teams to improve operational performance, eliminate waste, and build sustainable operating processes. The Senior Operations manager is also responsible for building and maintaining positive employee relations and developing leadership strength within the Distribution Center. This position operates under the general guidance of the Plant Manager. As the Senior Operations Manager, you will: Oversee warehouse operations including receiving, putaway, replenishment, picking, shipping, and inventory execution Drive safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity performance through disciplined daily management and KPI reviews Lead, coach, and develop managers of managers while fostering a culture of accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement Monitor operational performance using KPIs such as throughput, labor productivity, inventory accuracy, dock-to-stock, order accuracy, and on-time shipment Partner with Customer Service, Inventory, Transportation, and Materials to resolve operational constraints and improve customer service performance Drive root cause analysis and implement sustainable corrective actions for operational issues Ensure compliance with safety regulations, OSHA requirements, and company policies Oversee continuous improvement initiatives to optimize warehouse layout, material flow, labor utilization, and operating processes Develop and maintain standard work, operating procedures (SOPs), and operational controls Support peak planning, workforce planning, and resource allocation to meet business demands Lead additional projects and initiatives as assigned by the Plant Manager Required education, experiences & skills: Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, Operations, or a related field (or equivalent experience) 5+ years of direct management experience in leadership in warehouse, distribution center, or manufacturing operations Demonstrated experience leading managers and supervisors in a high-volume, metrics-driven environment Strong knowledge of warehouse operations, inventory management, and shipping/receiving processes Experience utilizing ERP and Warehouse Management Systems (Oracle, SAP, Manhattan, etc.) Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership skills Proven ability to drive operational improvements through data, standard work, and continuous improvement methodologies Preferred education, experiences & skills: Experience leading multi-shift distribution center operations Lean, Six Sigma, or Continuous Improvement experience Experience with Daily Management Systems (Tier meetings, KPI reviews, Leader Standard Work) Ability to handle changing priorities and use good judgement in multiple situations Knowledge of warehouse automation and material handling systems Experience leading change management and operational transformation initiatives OSHA knowledge and forklift safety certification preferred Why Work in the Dallas-Fort Worth Area Our distribution center is located in Forney, TX, one of the fastest-growing communities in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. Conveniently located just east of Dallas, Forney offers easy access to world-class dining, entertainment, professional sports, shopping, and cultural attractions throughout the DFW area. Residents enjoy a strong sense of community, highly rated schools, affordable housing options compared to many major metro areas, and a variety of parks, recreation, and family-friendly activities. About Our Location Our Forney Distribution Center plays a key role in supporting Copeland customers across North America through efficient warehousing, inventory management, and order fulfillment operations. The facility serves as a critical hub within our supply chain network, helping ensure the timely delivery of HVACR products and solutions to customers. Team members work closely across operations, customer service, materials, inventory, and transportation functions in a fast-paced, collaborative environment focused on safety, quality, and continuous improvement. As the site continues to grow, employees have opportunities to develop their skills and advance their careers within Copeland's global organization. title: IT Infrastructure Manager
jd_text: CrossCountry Mortgage (CCM) is the nation's number one distributed retail mortgage lender with more than 9,000 employees operating over 700 branches and servicing loans across all 50 states, D.C. and Puerto Rico. Position Overview: The IT Infrastructure Manager leads a team responsible for the engineering, delivery, modernization, and continuous improvement of CCM’s enterprise infrastructure platforms. This role is accountable for designing, building, and delivering secure, scalable, resilient, and supportable technology solutions across CCM’s hybrid infrastructure environment. This is a BUILD-focused leadership role responsible for infrastructure strategy, engineering standards, project delivery, automation, platform modernization, and operational readiness. The IT Infrastructure Manager partners closely with Enterprise Architecture, Security & Risk, Technology Operations, PMO, and business technology stakeholders to ensure infrastructure solutions are well-designed, well-documented, secure, repeatable, and ready for operational support. This role encompasses cloud infrastructure, on-premises infrastructure, network engineering, identity and access platforms, Microsoft 365 and collaboration foundations, endpoint platform foundations, automation, Infrastructure as Code, and enterprise platform delivery. Job Responsibilities: Develop and execute short- and long-term infrastructure roadmaps that support CCM’s business growth, technology modernization, and operational resilience. Translate enterprise technology objectives into practical infrastructure plans across hybrid cloud, AWS, Azure, networking, identity, endpoint foundations, collaboration platforms, and core enterprise services. Define and maintain infrastructure engineering standards, reference architectures, design patterns, documentation expectations, and operational readiness requirements. Drive scalable, repeatable infrastructure delivery through automation, Infrastructure as Code, standard templates, reusable patterns, and disciplined change management. Partner with Enterprise Architecture and Security & Risk to ensure infrastructure solutions align with enterprise architecture principles, security controls, compliance expectations, and business continuity requirements. Evaluate emerging technologies, vendors, services, tools, and delivery models that improve reliability, scalability, cost efficiency, security, and engineering velocity. Develop business cases, cost-benefit analyses, and recommendations for infrastructure investments, modernization initiatives, and platform improvements. Lead the design, engineering, and implementation of infrastructure solutions across CCM’s hybrid environment, including AWS, Azure, on-premises platforms, networking, identity/IAM, Microsoft 365, collaboration tools, and endpoint platform foundations. Oversee infrastructure project delivery from intake through design, implementation, testing, documentation, transition, and operational handoff. Ensure new infrastructure solutions are secure by design, observable, resilient, cost-conscious, supportable, and aligned with enterprise standards. Drive adoption of modern deployment practices, including Infrastructure as Code, Git-based workflows, CI/CD pipelines, automated configuration, scripting, and repeatable release patterns. Provide leadership for infrastructure modernization efforts, lifecycle management, cloud adoption, platform consolidation, technical debt reduction, and service improvement initiatives. Ensure infrastructure designs include appropriate monitoring, alerting, logging, backup, recovery, capacity, performance, and support requirements before transition to Operations. Partner with Technology Operations to ensure clean handoffs, clear runbooks, escalation paths, knowledge transfer, and operational support models. Manage engineering delivery across core infrastructure domains, including cloud platforms, network services, identity services, directory services, collaboration platforms, and enterprise productivity foundations. Support AWS as a required platform capability and Azure as a preferred platform capability, ensuring cloud environments are built with strong governance, security, resiliency, automation, and cost-management practices. Provide leadership across network engineering capabilities such as LAN/WAN, SD-WAN, VPN, DNS, DHCP, firewall coordination, connectivity, segmentation, cloud networking, and performance optimization. Guide identity and access platform initiatives involving Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, SSO, MFA, privileged access, conditional access, lifecycle management, and least-privilege access models. Support Microsoft 365 and collaboration platform foundations, including governance, platform configuration, security alignment, service enablement, and enterprise adoption needs. Partner with endpoint, security, and operations teams to ensure endpoint platform foundations are standardized, manageable, secure, and aligned with enterprise requirements. Partner with Security & Risk to embed security requirements into infrastructure designs, implementation plans, and operational readiness criteria. Ensure infrastructure platforms support appropriate controls for identity, access, logging, encryption, vulnerability management, patching, lifecycle management, backup, recovery, and resiliency. Support disaster recovery, business continuity, incident readiness, and infrastructure resilience planning. Participate in major incident reviews, root cause analysis, remediation planning, and continuous improvement activities as an infrastructure engineering leader. Ensure infrastructure documentation, architecture diagrams, standards, implementation records, and support procedures remain current and audit-ready. Establish strong delivery practices that balance speed, quality, security, supportability, and long-term maintainability. Maintain clear communication with IT leadership, project stakeholders, Technology Operations, Security & Risk, Enterprise Architecture, PMO, business partners, and vendors. Provide executive-ready updates on infrastructure initiatives, risks, delivery progress, resource needs, dependencies, and decision points. Define and track key performance indicators related to infrastructure delivery, platform health, project execution, technical debt reduction, automation, and operational readiness. Serve as an escalation point for complex infrastructure engineering issues, major production concerns, and high-priority platform decisions. Ensure infrastructure work is prioritized, planned, delivered, documented, and transitioned effectively. Lead, coach, and develop a team of infrastructure engineers and technical professionals. Set clear goals, priorities, standards, and expectations for team delivery, quality, documentation, collaboration, and accountability. Manage team capacity, resource planning, work assignments, performance feedback, hiring, onboarding, and professional development. Build a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, engineering discipline, service excellence, and cross-functional partnership. Promote knowledge sharing, standardization, mentoring, and repeatable delivery practices across the infrastructure team. Manage vendor relationships, technology evaluations, renewals, support agreements, and infrastructure-related procurement activities. Support infrastructure budget planning, forecasting, cloud cost management, licensing reviews, and cost optimization efforts. Partner with PMO and IT leadership to manage the infrastructure project portfolio, prioritize demand, identify delivery risks, and ensure alignment to enterprise objectives. Evaluate infrastructure investments based on business value, risk reduction, operational impact, scalability, security, and total cost of ownership. Participate in escalation support for major incidents, high-priority infrastructure issues, and critical production events. Occasional work outside standard business hours may be required to support planned maintenance, production changes, incident response, and project implementations. Qualifications and Skills: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. One or more industry-recognized certifications in cloud technologies, infrastructure automation, project management, cybersecurity, networking, endpoint management, or IT service management, preferred. 8+ years of progressive experience in infrastructure engineering, platform engineering, cloud infrastructure, network engineering, systems engineering, or related technology roles. 3+ years of experience leading infrastructure, platform, systems, network, or cloud engineering teams. Advanced experience delivering infrastructure solutions in a hybrid enterprise environment. Experience leading infrastructure projects from design through implementation, documentation, transition, and support readiness. Experience with Infrastructure as Code and automation tools such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Bicep, Ansible, PowerShell, Python, Bash, or similar technologies. Experience with CI/CD, Git-based workflows, release management, configuration management, and repeatable deployment practices. Experience with Microsoft 365, collaboration platforms, endpoint platform foundations, and enterprise productivity services. Experience with ITSM practices, change management, incident/problem management, operational readiness, and production support transition. Advanced experience in vendor management, budgeting, cost analysis, and infrastructure investment planning. Experience working in a regulated or security-conscious environment; financial services or mortgage industry experience, preferred. Advanced technical knowledge of AWS, Azure, hybrid infrastructure, virtualization, Windows and Linux server platforms, enterprise storage, backup/recovery, networking, and identity platforms. Advanced knowledge of Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, SSO, MFA, conditional access, privileged access, and identity lifecycle management. Knowledge of LAN/WAN, SD-WAN, DNS, DHCP, VPN, firewalls, routing, switching, load balancing, cloud networking, and network segmentation. Knowledge of AWS is required; Azure experience, preferred. Advanced understanding of infrastructure architecture, cloud architecture, networking, identity and access management, Microsoft enterprise platforms, automation, and operational support models. Advanced understanding of monitoring, logging, alerting, observability, capacity planning, performance management, and service reliability practices. Comfortable operating in a large, complex, and rapidly evolving organization. Skilled in leadership, strategic planning, decision-making, and driving execution to achieve business objectives. Skilled in communication, including communicating complex technical topics effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences. Skilled in partnering across Infrastructure, Operations, Security & Risk, Architecture, PMO, and business teams. Highly organized, delivery-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple priorities in a dynamic environment. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills. Skilled in evaluating and balancing competing priorities, including quality, security, cost, delivery timelines, and operational requirements. Skilled in aligning technology services with customer requirements, business objectives, and organizational reliability standards. Skilled in talent development, process improvement, standards enhancement, and building effective technical teams. title: Senior Systems Reliability Engineer
jd_text: At ERCOT, our diverse and dynamic work environment provides a platform on which employees can work together to build the future of the Texas power grid and wholesale market utilizing the latest technologies and resources. We encourage you to join our talented, dedicated workforce to develop world-class solutions for today and tomorrow’s energy challenges while learning new skills and growing your career. ERCOT is committed to fostering inclusion at all levels of our company. It is the cornerstone of our corporate values of accountability, leadership, innovation, trust, and expertise. We know that individuals with a wide variety of talents, ideas, and experiences propel the innovation that drives our success. An inclusive and diverse workforce strengthens us and allows for a collaborative environment to solve the challenges that face our industry today and in the future. JOB SUMMARY The Senior Systems Reliability Engineer applies software engineering discipline to reliability problems — designing, building, and operating the systems that make production software measurable, scalable, and self-healing. This role treats operational challenges as engineering problems: when a process is manual, it gets automated; when a failure mode is unknown, it gets instrumented; when a system degrades, the degradation is understood before it recurs. At this level, the specialist owns SLO and error budget frameworks for assigned systems, architects the observability stack that the team relies on, leads engineering-driven incident response, and holds NERC/CIP compliance responsibility for assigned systems. This role partners directly with Software Engineers as a technical peer — participating in design reviews, influencing architecture decisions for reliability, and building the production readiness standards that govern how software ships. Advancement to Lead is based on demonstrated ability to define reliability engineering standards at the platform level, influencing practice across multiple teams and portfolios. JOB DUTIES Performs complex reliability engineering work autonomously; recognized subject matter expert within the team and adjacent teams. Designs and builds production software systems, reliability tooling, and automation frameworks; treats operational problems as engineering problems to be solved through code. Owns SLO governance, error budget management, and observability architecture for assigned systems; leads engineering-driven incident response including failover scenarios. Holds NERC/CIP compliance responsibility for assigned systems; formally mentors less experienced specialists; may coordinate team delivery and on-call activities. ADDITIONAL JOB DUTIES Core Expectations The following expectations apply at all Systems Reliability Specialist levels. Scope and independence expand with each level. Engineer reliability solutions: when a process is manual and repeatable, automate it; when a failure mode is opaque, instrument it; when a system is fragile, redesign the failure boundary. Define and own SLIs and SLOs for assigned systems; treat error budgets as a shared engineering contract with development teams, not an operations metric. Respond to production incidents as an engineer: form a hypothesis, isolate the failure, resolve it, and close the loop with a post-mortem that addresses root cause. Instrument systems so that on-call responders have sufficient telemetry to diagnose and act without tribal knowledge. Participate in 24/7 on-call rotation; treat every alert as signal — either actionable or worth eliminating. Write production-quality code: reliability tooling, automation frameworks, and operational software are held to the same engineering standards as application code. Partner with development teams as a peer in design reviews; reliability is designed in, not bolted on after deployment. Reliability Engineering Senior specialists design and build the engineering systems that make production software reliable. This is software engineering applied to operational problems — the output is code, frameworks, and automated systems, not tickets and runbooks alone. Design, build, and maintain reliability tooling: automated remediation systems, self-healing infrastructure components, and operational software that reduces human intervention in production. Own SLO and error budget definitions for assigned systems; review error budget consumption with development teams and drive engineering decisions based on budget status. Architect and implement chaos engineering programs: define failure injection scenarios, automate resilience tests, and validate recovery behavior against defined SLOs. Build and maintain CI/CD reliability gates: automated canary analysis, progressive delivery validation, and rollback triggers based on SLI thresholds. Design capacity planning models for assigned systems; build tooling to project resource needs and surface capacity risks before they affect availability. Contribute to production readiness reviews: define and enforce the engineering criteria that a system must meet before it ships to production. Reduce operational toil through engineering: measure toil, track reduction targets, and build the automation that eliminates it. Observability & Instrumentation Observability is an engineering discipline. Senior specialists design and build the telemetry systems that make production behavior understandable — not just monitored. Architect MLTP (Metrics, Logs, Traces, Profiling) observability solutions using the Grafana LGTM stack (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir), Dynatrace APM, Splunk, and Datadog. Define and enforce instrumentation standards: structured logging schemas, metric naming conventions, trace context propagation, and continuous profiling configuration for assigned systems. Build distributed tracing coverage across service boundaries; identify and close observability gaps that produce blind spots during incidents. Design SLI instrumentation: translate user-facing reliability requirements into specific, measurable signals that accurately represent system health from the user's perspective. Build and maintain alerting frameworks: alerts must be actionable, calibrated to SLO burn rate, and free of noise; own alert quality as an engineering output. Correlate application performance data — JVM heap behavior, GC pressure, thread contention — with infrastructure events to enable root cause analysis across layers. Incident Response & Problem Management Incident response at this level is an engineering activity. Senior specialists lead the technical response to high-severity events, own the post-mortem process, and drive the engineering work that prevents recurrence. Lead high-severity incident response for assigned systems, including dual-datacenter failover execution; own the technical resolution from detection through remediation. Apply structured root cause analysis: distinguish symptoms from causes, identify contributing factors across system layers, and drive remediation that addresses root cause rather than surface behavior. Author post-mortems that produce actionable engineering work items — not process improvements alone; track remediation to completion and validate effectiveness. Diagnose complex cross-layer failures: Java/JVM application failures, distributed system race conditions, database connection pool exhaustion, messaging system backpressure, and cross-datacenter synchronization issues. Build and maintain incident response runbooks as engineering artifacts: automated where feasible, version-controlled, and validated during chaos engineering exercises. Participate in blameless post-mortem facilitation; model the engineering culture that treats incidents as system failures, not human failures. Java Application Reliability The primary application platform is Java/Spring Boot. Senior specialists are expected to operate at the intersection of application engineering and reliability — understanding the runtime deeply enough to diagnose, tune, and improve production behavior. Diagnose and resolve Java application performance problems in production: heap memory pressure, garbage collection tuning, thread pool exhaustion, connection leak detection, and class loading anomalies. Perform JVM performance analysis using heap dumps, thread dumps, and continuous profiling; translate findings into engineering recommendations for development teams. Instrument Spring Boot applications with production-grade observability: Micrometer metrics, structured logging with correlation IDs, and distributed trace integration. Diagnose failures across the Java application stack: Spring Boot service behavior, PostgreSQL and Oracle query performance, Kafka and ActiveMQ messaging reliability, and REST/SOAP API integration failures. Contribute to Java application design reviews with a reliability lens: identify failure modes, single points of failure, and observability gaps before code ships to production. Platform & Infrastructure Engineering Senior specialists build and maintain the platform engineering components that reliability depends on — container orchestration, infrastructure automation, deployment tooling, and environment governance. Design and operate Kubernetes and OpenShift workloads for reliability: resource quotas, pod disruption budgets, horizontal pod autoscaling, and liveness and readiness probe engineering. Build infrastructure-as-code for reliability infrastructure: Terraform modules, Ansible/AAP playbooks, and Azure Resource Manager templates that are tested, version-controlled, and peer-reviewed. Own dual-datacenter reliability architecture for assigned systems: synchronization validation, automated failover triggering, traffic management, and recovery time objective verification. Design and automate environment promotion pipelines: ensure that configuration, secrets, and infrastructure state are consistent and validated across development, test, staging, and production. Build and maintain automated patch compliance workflows; integrate CVE remediation into CI/CD pipelines rather than treating it as a manual operational process. NERC/CIP Compliance NERC/CIP compliance for assigned systems is an engineering responsibility at this level — not a documentation exercise. Senior specialists implement controls through code and automation wherever possible. Own NERC/CIP compliance for assigned systems: interpret applicable reliability standards, implement required controls, maintain evidence documentation, and prepare for regulatory audit. Engineer compliance controls into the platform where possible: automated hardening scripts, configuration drift detection, access control validation, and audit log integrity verification. Maintain currency on applicable NERC/CIP standards and ERCOT-specific regulatory requirements; escalate emerging compliance risks to the Lead or Manager. Participate in regulatory audit preparation: produce control evidence, respond to auditor inquiries, and coordinate with compliance stakeholders on findings remediation. Technical Leadership & Mentoring Hold formal mentoring responsibility for Systems Reliability Specialist I and II team members: structured coaching on SRE practices, code review for reliability tooling, and career development conversations. title: Grid Interconnections Engineer 2
jd_text: At ERCOT, our diverse and dynamic work environment provides a platform on which employees can work together to build the future of the Texas power grid and wholesale market utilizing the latest technologies and resources. We encourage you to join our talented, dedicated workforce to develop world-class solutions for today and tomorrow’s energy challenges while learning new skills and growing your career. ERCOT is committed to fostering inclusion at all levels of our company. It is the cornerstone of our corporate values of accountability, leadership, innovation, trust, and expertise. We know that individuals with a wide variety of talents, ideas, and experiences propel the innovation that drives our success. An inclusive and diverse workforce strengthens us and allows for a collaborative environment to solve the challenges that face our industry today and in the future. JOB SUMMARY Manages the interconnection process for stand-alone Large Loads, from initial application through energization, and for co-located projects (a Resource or Energy Storage Resource (ESR) paired with a Large Load) from initial application through approval for commercial operations. For co-located projects, responsibilities include performing security screening studies, reviewing Full Interconnection Study (FIS) scope and study reports, reviewing the Standard Generation Interconnection Agreement (SGIA), and reviewing Commissioning Plans and Energization, Synchronization, and Commissioning checklists. Performs regular and ad-hoc analyses of large load consumption behavior and its impact on the reliability of the ERCOT interconnection. Develops appropriate tools, dashboards, policies, and procedures to ensure reliable integration of large loads and co-located resources. Serves as a subject matter expert on large load and co-located resource topics to ERCOT management and other ERCOT teams. JOB DUTIES Engineer 1 Manages, reviews and performs necessary analysis for the interconnection process for stand-alone large loads (initial application through energization) and co-located projects (initial application through approval for commercial operation). Reviews and processes co-located project interconnection and FIS applications; may review Reactive Study reports, FIS scope and reports, and Standard Generation Interconnection Agreements. Performs powerflow and security screening studies to assess the reliability of co-located interconnection requests. May review commissioning testing data for co-located Resources/ESRs (e.g., AVR/PSS and Reactive tests). May review and approve modeling data for the planning phase of the interconnection process and in the Operations model. Ensures that the interconnection of large loads projects and co-located projects is accomplished in a manner that maintains the reliability of the ERCOT System and complies with NERC Reliability Standards, ERCOT Protocols, the Planning Guide, and the Operating Guides. Supports periodic testing of operational resources to confirm continued compliance with interconnection and performance requirements. Works closely with ERCOT System Operations, System Operations Support, Market Operating Services Support, Client Services, System Planning and Metering. Works closely with Market Participants (MPs), including Interconnecting Entities (IEs), Resource Entities (REs), Distribution Service Providers (DSPs), and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs). Performs regular and ad-hoc analyses of large load behavior and impacts on ERCOT markets and real-time reliability Gains knowledge of relevant market rules and departmental procedures Engineer 2 Perform all duties of an Engineer 1, as well as the following. Participates in cross-functional teams to ensure large loads are fully integrated into ERCOT models and systems Is proficient in market rules and departmental procedures Develops, enhances, and maintains tools and reports for ERCOT stakeholders that improve visibility and understanding of large load activity EXPERIENCE Engineer 1 Requires no additional job related work experience in excess of degree requirements (Required) Ability to communicate effectively (Required) Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint experience (Preferred) Experience developing situational awareness tools and/or coding Engineer 2 Requires minimum 1 year job related work experience in excess of degree requirements (Required) Ability to communicate effectively (Required) Ability to read and understand electrical one lines and drawings (Required) Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint experience (Preferred) Experience performing and evaluating powerflow studies in transmission or distribution systems (Preferred) Experience developing situational awareness tools and/or coding (Preferred) Experience with Seeq, PI, and/or Jira Salary and level will be based on overall experience as determined by ERCOT Senior Engineer requires 5 more years of relevant experience EDUCATION Bachelor's Degree : Electrical Engineering or related field (Required) or a combination of education and experience that provides equivalent knowledge to a major in such fields is required CERTIFICATION PE Professional Engineer (Preferred) ERCOT is firmly committed to equal employment for all qualified persons without regard to race, sex, medical condition, religion, age, creed, national origin, citizenship status, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, ancestry, veteran status, genetic information or any other protected category under federal, state or local law. Expected Salary Range: $89,000 - $122,000

The manager partners daily with cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, project management, IT operations, and DevOps. The strongest candidates bring depth in several technical domains, familiarity across the rest, and a track record of growing people and leading through influence. JOB DUTIES Lead, coach, and develop a team of application and solution architects—hiring, onboarding, performance management, career development, and cross-training. Build the monthly capacity forecast projecting each architect’s time across projects, operations, training, and time off, and provide it to the project team for capacity planning. Assign and balance work across the team, resolve competing project and operational demands, and escalate when demand exceeds capacity. Lead the evolution of the IT solutions architecture function—its processes, deliverables, governance, and standards. Contribute to ERCOT’s IT strategic plan and translate it into actionable architecture roadmaps. Assess the current IT environment for deficiencies, technical debt, and risk, and recommend prioritized remediation. Oversee the technical and business roadmaps, reference architectures, and design deliverables the team produces. Review and approve solution designs for alignment with enterprise architecture, security, and operational supportability. Direct the standards-setting process, lead the architecture standards committee, and maintain the principles governing technology investment. Evaluate emerging technologies, including AI and cloud, and set practical guardrails for the team’s use of AI-assisted tooling. Partner with cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, the project team, IT operations, and DevOps on security requirements, enterprise alignment, resource planning, and supportable designs. Develop vendor strategies, contribute to build versus buy decisions, and provide input to departmental budgeting. SKILLS & EXPERIENCE Technical Expertise Minimum 8 years of job-related work experience and 2 years in a leadership role in excess of degree requirements. Minimum years of job-related experience can include time in leadership roles. Experience in at least two IT disciplines—such as solution architecture, application development, data management, or IT operations—supporting a 24x7 environment. Strong foundation in application and integration architecture, distributed systems, and API design. Hands-on experience designing or operating workloads in a major public cloud. Working knowledge of identity and access management, DevOps, CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code, observability, and AI-assisted development tools. Working understanding of security architecture, networking, and governance frameworks, and how compliance obligations shape design decisions. Depth to review designs critically and arbitrate technical disagreements, plus experience establishing architecture standards and driving adoption. Leadership & Collaboratio n Proven experience leading a technical team, including hiring, coaching, performance management, and career development. Track record of building capacity forecasts and using them to set realistic commitments. Ability to balance competing priorities across projects and operations, and renegotiate scope with clear reasoning. Skill in developing people—growth plans and cross-training so knowledge is not concentrated in one person. Ability to lead through influence, give direct feedback, and handle difficult conversations with candor. Strong communication, with proven partnership across cybersecurity, enterprise architecture, project management, IT operations, and DevOps, and credibility with IT and business leadership. QUALIFICATIONS Hands-on experience with cloud architecture and governance at enterprise scale, preferably Azure. Relevant cloud certifications are a plus. Experience introducing AI capabilities and AI-assisted tooling into an engineering organization. Experience in grid, market, or transmission operations, at an ISO/RTO, or applying NERC CIP to solution design. Background in enterprise transformation, modernization, or platform engineering programs. EDUCATION Bachelor’s Degree: Computer Science, MIS or related field (Required) Master’s Degree: Computer Science, MIS or related field (Preferred) or a combination of education and experience that provides equivalent knowledge to a major in such fields is required CERTIFICATION CISSP Certified Information Systems Security Professional (Preferred) PMP Project Management Professional (Preferred) TOGAF (Preferred) WORK LOCATION Hybrid in Taylor, TX 2 days per week The foregoing description reflects the minimum qualifications and the essential functions of the position that must be performed proficiently with or without reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities. title: Data Operations Administrator III
jd_text: At Exeter Finance, we are committed to helping customers find the right financing for their next vehicle purchase. Our vision is to be a premier finance company and lender of choice known for its People, Performance and Service. Job Description Job Summary This position is hybrid and will be required to be in office two times per month for collaboration working sessions. The Data Operations Administrator III delivers high availability enterprise job scheduling solutions by proactively monitoring and administering scheduling platforms to ensure consistent system performance. Maintains operational stability through timely resolution of planned and unplanned job failures and partnership with cross-functional technical teams. Enhances scheduling reliability by applying technical expertise, optimizing processes, and supporting operational objectives. Job Duties • Design, implement, and maintain the enterprise job scheduling environment to support multiple applications and ensure high system availability. • Monitor scheduling workflows, diagnose failures, and resolve incidents by partnering with users, internal teams, and vendors to identify root causes and restore functionality. • Administer job scheduling tools and follow standardized procedures—ensuring adherence to project methodologies, operational processes, and service-level commitments. • Manage file transfer and encryption processes, including troubleshooting and validating file movement across systems. • Participate in a 24/7 on-call rotation, providing after-hours support to meet operational availability requirements and quickly address system failures. • Perform data-related ad hoc tasks such as research, file manipulation, and process review to support business needs. • Collaborate with application developers, operations, and project managers to build scalable, maintainable scheduling solutions and continuously improve performance. • Maintain compliance with IT Risk, Incident, Problem, and Change Management controls and ensure consistent documentation and tracking through the ticketing system. Education and Experience • Bachelor’s degree or educational experience in related field preferred, or relevant work experience. • 4-6 years experience with Enterprise Job Scheduling/Orchestration solutions, such as ActiveBatch, Control-M, Autosys, etc. • 4-6 years of experience working with cross-functional teams and managing large-scale project budgets, timelines, and resources. • Extensive experience in data operations management, including data pipeline design, data integration, and managing large-scale data environments. • Advanced knowledge of database systems (SQL, NoSQL), data warehousing solutions, and cloud data platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP). • Expertise in ETL tools and platforms (e.g., Talend, Informatica, Apache Nifi) and experience optimizing their use for large-scale data workflows. • Strong experience with data governance, data security, and compliance standards such as GDPR, HIPAA, and other relevant regulations. • Proficiency in scripting and automation tools (e.g., Python, SQL, Bash) to streamline data operations and improve efficiency. • Proven ability to lead and manage complex data operations projects, working collaboratively with technical teams and business units to achieve objectives. • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to resolve complex data-related issues and implement sustainable solutions. • Strong leadership abilities, including mentoring and guiding junior staff and fostering a collaborative and efficient work environment. • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders at all levels of the organization. • Strong analytical skills with the ability to assess system performance, identify areas for improvement, and optimize data operations. #LI-Hybrid Individual compensation packages are based on various factors unique to each candidate including skill set, experience, qualifications and other job-related reasons. title: Member Growth Operations Associate Manager
jd_text: Virta Health is on a mission to reverse metabolic disease in one billion people. Current treatment approaches aren’t working—over half of US adults have either type 2 diabetes or prediabetes, and obesity rates are at an all-time high. Virta is changing this by helping people reverse their metabolic condition through innovations in technology, personalized nutrition, and virtual care delivery reinvented from the ground up. We have raised over $350 million from top-tier investors, and partner with the largest health plans, employers, and government organizations to help their employees and members restore their health and take back their lives. Join us on our mission to reverse metabolic disease in one billion people. Virta Health is seeking a Member Growth Operations Manager to help evolve how we deliver member communications across email, direct mail, and SMS. As we build toward more personalized member journeys, we are improving the data, systems, and workflows that power our campaigns—with Braze at the center. In this role, you will help turn that strategy into day-to-day capabilities: reusable campaign components, dynamic content, automated workflows, and reliable processes that support more relevant outreach at scale. You will partner with Growth, Data, Engineering, and Implementation teams to translate business and client needs into operational requirements and bring new capabilities into use. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with ownership of both campaign delivery and operational improvement. You will execute and maintain current programs while helping build the systems that enable our next stage of growth. It is an opportunity to shape how a team works, see your improvements put into practice, and grow as our capabilities evolve. HOW YOU WILL WORK You connect the details of campaign execution to the broader member experience and business goal. You are comfortable navigating ambiguity, identifying the root cause of recurring problems, and deciding when to improve an existing process or build a more scalable approach. You take work from requirements through implementation, testing, documentation, and adoption—and help teammates use what you build. RESPONSIBILITIES Own campaign execution and operational readiness - Independently manage assigned ongoing campaigns and launch work across email, direct mail, and SMS, including configuration, timelines, approvals, vendor coordination, and delivery. - Build and update Braze campaigns and Canvases, maintain client-specific content and catalog data, and support accurate application of contact preferences and suppression rules. - Lead end-to-end QA of content, dynamic logic, audience criteria, links, and technical configuration; troubleshoot issues and strengthen controls to prevent recurrence. - Translate custom communication requests into clear requirements and execution plans, identifying opportunities to meet those needs through reusable solutions. - Document issues, communicate risks early, and help strengthen QA controls based on lessons learned. Drive continuous improvement across the team - Own operational improvement projects from problem definition through rollout, managing dependencies and communicating decisions, tradeoffs, and risks. - Partner with Growth stakeholders to turn campaign learnings and member behavior into improvements to targeting, journeys, and execution. - Define and track measures of operational success, such as reduced manual effort, faster campaign setup, fewer errors, and more reliable delivery. - Provide hands-on coverage as priorities shift and build shared knowledge that reduces reliance on any one person. - Use AI to streamline campaign operations, strengthen QA, and reduce manual work—applying sound judgment to validate outputs and build reliable, scalable workflows. 90 DAY PLAN Within your first 90 days at Virta, we expect you will do the following: - Develop a working understanding of our campaign systems, data dependencies, client requirements, QA standards, and transformation priorities. - Independently own assigned campaign workflows, delivering accurate, timely communications and managing dependencies across partners. - Assess an assigned workflow and recommend prioritized improvements based on member and client impact, manual effort, and implementation complexity. - Implement and document at least one reusable component or workflow improvement, validate it through QA, and establish a way to measure its impact. MUST-HAVES - 5–7 years of relevant experience in marketing operations, lifecycle operations, marketing technology, or a related field, with independent ownership of complex campaigns and operational improvements. - Demonstrated experience building and maintaining scalable workflows in Braze or a comparable customer engagement platform, including automation, segmentation, and dynamic content. - Ability to translate business needs into system and data requirements, partner effectively with technical teams, and validate campaign logic and data quality through disciplined QA. - Strong project ownership and communication skills, with the judgment to prioritize improvements alongside ongoing delivery, manage dependencies, and guide teammates through changes. - Successfully designed and implemented repeatable AI-enabled workflows that address team bottlenecks and improve efficiency. For more information about AI usage in our hiring process, see Virta’s AI Interview Resources https://www.virtahealth.com/careers/ai-interview-resources page. NICE TO HAVE - Hands-on experience with Braze Canvases, Catalogs, Content Blocks, and Liquid personalization. - Familiarity with HTML/CSS, SQL, APIs, or data integrations used to build, validate, or troubleshoot marketing workflows. - Experience supporting direct mail or SMS programs, including vendor coordination and cross-channel contact rules. - Experience with healthcare, benefits, or other environments with complex eligibility, client-specific requirements, and sensitive data. VALUES-DRIVEN CULTURE Virta’s company values drive our culture, so you’ll do well if: - You put people first and take care of yourself, your peers, and our patients equally - You have a strong sense of ownership and take initiative while empowering others to do the same - You prioritize positive impact over busy work - You have no ego and understand that everyone has something to bring to the table regardless of experience - You appreciate transparency and promote trust and empowerment through open access of information - You are evidence-based and prioritize data and science over seniority or dogma - You take risks and rapidly iterate Is this role not quite what you're looking for? Join our Talent Community https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/virtahealth/form/talent-community-form and follow us on Linkedin https://www.linkedin.com/company/virta-health to stay connected! Virta has a location based compensation structure. Starting pay will be based on a number of factors and commensurate with qualifications & experience. For this role, the compensation range is $99,500 to $128,500. Information about Virta’s benefits is on our Careers page at: https://www.virtahealth.com/careers. As part of your duties at Virta, you may come in contact with sensitive patient information that is governed by HIPAA. Throughout your career at Virta, you will be expected to follow Virta's security and privacy procedures to ensure our patients' information remains strictly confidential. Security and privacy training will be provided. As a remote-first company, our team is spread across various locations with office hubs in Denver and San Francisco. Clinical roles: We currently do not hire in the following states: AK, HI, RI Corporate roles: We currently do not hire in the following states: AK, DE, HI, ME, MS, OK, SD, VT. Virta uses Ashby as its applicant tracking system, which incorporates AI-powered tools (provided by OpenAI, AWS, and Google Gemini) in certain aspects of the recruiting process, including application review, candidate screening, and interview note taking; your data is not used to train AI models, and all final hiring decisions are made by Virta Health personnel. For more information, see Virta’s AI Interview Resources page. https://www.virtahealth.com/careers/ai-interview-resources

title: Managing Consultant, Environmental Permitting Project Manager
jd_text: Lead the Delivery of Complex Energy Projects That Shape the Future ERM is seeking a Managing Consultant, Project Manager to join our growing Capital Project Delivery Team in the Gulf Coast region (Texas) . This is an outstanding opportunity for an experienced project leader who thrives at the intersection of environmental permitting, infrastructure development, and strategic client advisory services. In this highly visible, client-facing role, you will guide complex capital projects from concept through execution, helping clients navigate regulatory challenges, manage risk, and deliver critical investments across the oil and gas, LNG, power, renewable energy, low carbon, and energy transition sectors. If you're energized by leading multidisciplinary teams, influencing major project outcomes, and contributing to the future of energy development, this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact. Why This Role Matters As organizations invest in critical infrastructure and energy transition initiatives, successful project delivery depends on strong leadership, regulatory expertise, and effective risk management. In this role, you will serve as a trusted advisor to clients, helping them navigate complex permitting processes, environmental impact assessments, and project delivery challenges while advancing sustainable and responsible development. You will play a key role in strengthening ERM's presence within the Diversified Energy sector, managing high-profile projects, supporting business growth, and collaborating with experts across ERM's national Low Carbon Energy Transition (LCET) network. Your work will directly contribute to both project success and ERM's broader global strategy. What Your Impact Is Lead the successful delivery of capital development projects across the energy sector by managing scope, schedules, budgets, quality, and project risk. Provide strategic permitting and environmental impact assessment guidance for complex infrastructure and energy projects. Serve as a trusted client advisor throughout project lifecycles, from proposal development through project execution and delivery. Support the advancement of low carbon and energy transition projects that are reshaping the industry. Strengthen client relationships while identifying opportunities to expand services and support commercial growth. Help develop and mentor team members while contributing to a collaborative, high-performing project environment. Influence the successful delivery of projects involving oil and gas pipelines, LNG facilities, low carbon capital development, solar, onshore wind, offshore wind, energy storage, and transmission. What You'll Bring Required Bachelor's or Master's degree in Environmental Science, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience. 4+ years of experience in either a consulting environment or working substantially within the energy sector. Demonstrated project management and leadership skills. Experience managing projects with multidisciplinary teams and balancing multiple priorities, workstreams, and deadlines. Experience managing and performing multi-media permitting associated with capital development projects. Strong understanding of local, state, and federal permitting requirements and regulatory processes. Demonstrated understanding of the energy regulatory environment, key regulatory agencies, and current and emerging issues. Strong analytical, technical writing, presentation, and client communication skills. Attention to detail and commitment to delivering high-quality work products. Ability to work independently while leading project teams and driving project execution. Experience supporting commercial success through identifying client opportunities, proposal development, and cross-selling multidisciplinary services. Experience with line management and/or contributing to the professional development of team members. Enthusiasm, initiative, flexibility, and a desire to work within a growing team. Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area. This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. Preferred 7+ years of experience in either a consulting environment or working substantially within the energy sector. Impact Assessment expertise, including NEPA EA/EIS, FERC, or similar agency experience. USACE and NEPA expertise, including experience with FERC permitting and EIS development. Familiarity with Texas and Louisiana state permitting requirements. ESHIA (Environmental, Social, and Health Impact Assessment) experience. Understanding of ERM's Diversified Energy Sector and the companies operating in this market, including existing relationships that can be leveraged into new business. Key Responsibilities Support and help manage large, complex, multidisciplinary, and global projects. Demonstrate strong project management leadership throughout the project lifecycle, including project scoping, budget management, scheduling, and delivery oversight. Manage and perform multi-media permitting associated with capital development projects, with an emphasis on local, state, and federal permitting requirements. Ensure compliance with regulations administered by agencies such as: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) Provide technical, subject matter, and project management expertise related to: Permitting strategies Due diligence reviews Environmental critical issues assessments Impact assessment deliverables Quality control reviews Apply strong analytical thinking and problem-solving skills to complex project challenges. Prepare and deliver high-quality technical reports, presentations, and client communications. Build and maintain strong, trusted relationships with clients and business partners. Contribute to proposal development, project pursuits, and broader business development initiatives. Who We Are: As the largest global pure play sustainability consultancy, we partner with the world’s leading organizations, creating innovative solutions to sustainability challenges and unlocking commercial opportunities that meet the needs of today while preserving opportunity for future generations. At ERM we know that creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment is an essential part of making our company a great place to build a career. We also see our diversity as a strength that helps us create better solutions for our clients. Our diverse team of world-class experts supports clients across the breadth of their organizations to operationalize sustainability, underpinned by our deep technical expertise in addressing their environmental, health, safety, risk and social issues. We call this capability our “boots to boardroom” approach for its comprehensive service model that allows ERM to develop strategic and technical solutions that advance objectives on the ground or at the executive level. ERM is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes. ERM is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. title: GMS Applications Developer - RIOO
jd_text: At ERCOT, our diverse and dynamic work environment provides a platform on which employees can work together to build the future of the Texas power grid and wholesale market utilizing the latest technologies and resources. We encourage you to join our talented, dedicated workforce to develop world-class solutions for today and tomorrow’s energy challenges while learning new skills and growing your career. ERCOT is committed to fostering inclusion at all levels of our company. It is the cornerstone of our corporate values of accountability, leadership, innovation, trust, and expertise. We know that individuals with a wide variety of talents, ideas, and experiences propel the innovation that drives our success. An inclusive and diverse workforce strengthens us and allows for a collaborative environment to solve the challenges that face our industry today and in the future. Grid and Market Solutions (GMS) Application Developer role expects knowledge and experience in full stack development who can design, code, test, document, and maintain applications to meet ERCOT business requirements for suite of Electric Power Grid Applications. The suite includes Resource Integration and Ongoing Operations (RIOO) system and Net Dependable Capability and Reactive Capability (NDCRC) web applications. Adhere to software development life cycle (SDLC) processes that include full stack development, performing testing and validation of Application to deliver quality software to customers. Works closely with customers, business area subject matter experts, team members and other internal technical teams to design, develop and maintain complex ERCOT applications in support of market needs and internal corporate requirements. Uses toolsets that adhere to the frameworks of the technical stack used across the GMS division and ensures that products and solutions comply with the organization’s architectural standards JOB DUTIES Broadly applies principles, theories and concepts related to the profession. A seasoned, experienced professional with an in-depth/full understanding of area of specialization. May provide recommendations regarding issues outside the bounds of defined procedures and practices. Demonstrates good judgment in selecting methods and techniques for obtaining solutions. Wide latitude for decisions within assignments, programs, and projects; impact is generally limited to the project or department. Acts as a resource to advise and may at times a lead the work of lower-level professional and/or support employees. Generally, represents the department on projects and may perform in a project leadership role. ADDITIONAL JOB DUTIES Performs all work according to applicable rules and regulations, including regulatory requirements and organizational policies and procedures. Works closely with business users and internal stakeholders to gather, review, and understand functional and non-functional requirements, proposing design improvements where appropriate. Designs, develops, tests, and maintains web-based applications using front-end and/or back-end technologies. Participates in requirements, design, and architecture review discussions with business users and technical teams. Develops and manages source code using Atlassian Bitbucket source control tools. Adheres to Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) standards and change management processes for all software releases. Understands and follows GMS application release processes and best practices to deliver software changes seamlessly. Participates in interdepartmental meetings and presents software design, implementation details, and application enhancements. Analyzes, troubleshoots, and resolves application issues by performing root cause analysis and delivering software solutions. Participates in developing design specifications that comply with ERCOT architectural standards and blueprints. Researches, evaluates, and incorporates new technologies and tools to improve product development and engineering efficiency. Resolves customer issues and responds to enhancement requests. Assists in developing product user manuals and technical documentation. Works closely with GMS Production Support and other teams to provide technical support for supported applications. Automates software development processes using CI/CD tools such as Bitbucket, Maven, and Jenkins. Assists in developing tools, processes, and procedures that improve software development and organizational efficiency. Leverages AI tools such as GitHub Copilot, GPT, and Claude to accelerate software development, testing, code quality, and engineering productivity. Works with data sets and data pipelines, including Airflow and Databricks, and analyzes third-party software security vulnerabilities to implement security patches. Performs code reviews and promotes coding standards, best practices, and design patterns. Performs manual and automated unit, regression, and integration testing using appropriate testing frameworks. Works closely with project management teams to ensure successful delivery of application changes through testing and production deployment. Collaborates with project managers, architects, developers, usability engineers, business users, market participants, vendors, and other stakeholders to ensure quality product delivery. Assists in providing development metrics, code statistics, and implementation of standardized development methodologies. Ensures products and solutions comply with organizational architectural standards. Focuses on application and system design while providing technical guidance and mentoring to team members. Partners with technical leads to define solutions for complex business problems and enforce engineering standards. Optimizes applications, leads root cause analysis for production issues, and drives automation initiatives. Organizes and coordinates application planning, design, architecture, development, testing, and integration activities. Advises management on technical direction and development goals for the GMS Technology Development team. Assists with project planning and delivery across all phases of application development. Serves as a Subject Matter Expert (SME), advising, mentoring, and guiding team members and cross-functional stakeholders. Communicates effectively through strong written and verbal communication skills. Works on moderately complex issues requiring in-depth analysis and creative problem-solving. Level Lead (In Addition to Senior) Provides strategic technical leadership and cross-team coordination. Establishes engineering standards, architectural patterns, and evaluates emerging technologies. Serves as the primary technical partner for Business/Product Owners, translating strategic goals into technical roadmaps. Drives a culture of innovation, technical excellence, and engineering best practices across multiple teams. Assists engineering teams in resolving complex technical challenges and delivering effective solutions. Mentors senior developers in software engineering best practices, object-oriented design, design patterns, and application frameworks. Maintains expert knowledge of ERCOT Nodal Protocols, PUCT rulings, NERC Reliability Standards, and CIP requirements, and mentors staff on regulatory compliance. All Levels -- Preferred SKILLS Messaging Services: Tibco JMS, AMQ, KAFKA Experience with CIM/XML model-based tools. Power industry experience in grid and market arena preferably with software vendors or ISO/utilities. AI: Proficiency in Python, knowledge in ML fundamentals, PyTorch/TensorFlow frameworks, experience with deep learning models, hands-on experience with LLM’s, prompt engineering and RAG architecture/frameworks.
