title: Digital Marketing Manager
jd_text: <p>Array is a financial innovation platform that helps digital brands, financial institutions, and fintechs get compelling consumer products to market faster. We deliver a suite of credit and identity monitoring tools, privacy protection, and a financial ads marketplace via embeddable widgets or a clean, modern API. Our private label offerings help drive revenue and increase engagement for our customers while empowering millions of consumers to achieve their financial goals.</p> <p>As a remote-first company, we’re focused on providing opportunities for high performing individuals to have deep impact in the fast growing fintech space. A clear mission, a commitment to continuous improvement and a willingness to experiment empower us individually and together deliver the best products for our clients and users.</p> <p>As a Digital Marketing Manager at Array, you will be our in-house performance marketing engine — you do what a full-service agency would do, except you sit inside the GTM team, know our verticals, and are accountable to pipeline. This role reports to the Head of Marketing.</p> <p><strong>The role</strong></p> <p>You’re the person in the ad platforms, in the CMS, in the analytics. Every program you run has a goal attached: net new customers, retention, or land-and-expand. If it can’t be tied to one of those, it doesn’t run.</p> <p><strong>You will:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Paid media — strategy and execution. </strong>Own Google Ads and LinkedIn end to end: account structure, budgets, bids, audiences, creative testing, and performance. Targeting aligned to our Tier 1/Tier 2 must-get accounts and five verticals. You build it, you run it, you hold the number.</li> <li><strong>SEO and AI search — </strong>Build our organic program from a standing start: technical foundation, on-page work, keyword strategy mapped by vertical, and optimizing for how buyers actually search now (traditional rankings and AI/answer-engine visibility). You write the briefs; content production supports you.</li> <li><strong>Top-of-funnel demand — </strong>Own the programs that fill the top of the funnel: search and social capture, content syndication, retargeting, and the paid layer under our ABM motion into must-get accounts.</li> <li><strong>Landing pages and conversion —&nbsp;</strong>Own the conversion layer of the site: landing pages, A/B testing, form and funnel optimization, and our Qualified chatbot (routing through Salesforce). You own what converts.</li> <li><strong>Measurement —&nbsp;</strong>Own tracking and reporting for everything above: UTM discipline, Salesforce campaign hygiene, and a pipeline-by-channel view.&nbsp;</li> <li>Work in the platforms daily. No vendor sits between you and the data.</li> <li>Report digital’s contribution to pipeline by vertical, in the same terms sales uses.</li> <li>Cut spend on programs that aren’t working, including the ones you built.</li> <li>Act on what you find the same week when able — a new audience, a rebuilt page, a tracking fix.</li> <li>Maintain a habit of using AI tools to think, build, and ship faster — it’s your default, not an afterthought.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Who you’ll work with</strong></p> <ul> <li>Demand Gen, Sales and our Vertical Marketing Managers — your programs feed their pods, and account lists shape your targeting.</li> <li>Marketing Ops and RevOps — your partners on routing, attribution, and Salesforce campaign hygiene.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What great looks like</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>90 days in: </strong>you own paid spend end to end — accounts audited, broken campaigns rebuilt, underperforming spend cut. Baseline SEO is in place (technical audit, keyword map by vertical, first briefs out) and testing is running on the top conversion paths.</li> <li><strong>6 months in: </strong>leadership uses your pipeline dashboard in planning. Organic traffic is growing. Sales can point to deals that started with a program you ran.</li> </ul> <p><strong>You have:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years running performance marketing hands-on for B2B, with real budget ownership — you’ve planned spend, defended it, and moved it when the data said to. Agency background is strongly welcome; you’ve run multiple client accounts and want to go deep on one.</li> <li>Platform fluency you can prove: Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, GA4, Google Tag Manager, and a CRM/MAP stack (we run Salesforce and HubSpot; we also use, ZoomInfo, and Gong).</li> <li>Real SEO chops: you can run a technical audit, brief content, and explain search visibility — including AI search — to an executive without jargon.</li> <li>CRO experience with testing frameworks, not just hunches.</li> <li>A pipeline-first mindset: you talk in opportunities and revenue influenced, not just impressions.</li> <li>Strong project management and communication — you can run multiple campaigns and stakeholders at once with clear briefs, tight timelines, and no dropped threads.</li> <li>Comfort as a team of one with agency-sized scope — this is a build role in a fast-moving GTM org, and you’d rather own the whole engine than a slice of it.</li> <li>A belief that AI is reshaping work — you instinctively use it to accelerate everything you do: analysis, reporting, briefs, creative iteration. Our team builds this way; you should too.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to have:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Fintech experience or selling into financial institutions.</li> <li>ABM platform experience and tiered account strategy.</li> <li>Experience marketing embedded/API products or private label offerings.</li> <li>Background in growth, social, or partner marketing alongside paid — you’ve pulled more than one lever.</li> <li>Experience with behavioral and intent data for targeting (we use ZoomInfo intent).</li> <li>Enough design/creative sense to brief ad creative well.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Pay transparency: </strong>$160,000 + for base salary, depending on experience. Success means meeting defined performance standards through a six-month evaluation period — with continuous feedback and ongoing accountability as core parts of working at Array.</p> <p><strong>Array Offers All Full Time Employees the following Benefits and Perks:&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Full medical, dental, and vision, premiums covered at 100% for full-time employees and 70% for dependents</li> <li>Unlimited PTO and sick leave + 14 company holidays to encourage a healthy work-life blend</li> <li>100% 401k match up to 4% with immediate vesting</li> <li>Generous and competitive parental leave for all parents</li> <li>$1,000 desk setup subsidy to set-up your unique remote office</li> <li>$100/month to subsidize wifi/cell phone expenses</li> <li>Summer Fridays (half-day Fridays) typically from late May to the end of August</li> <li>Commuter benefits for those who choose to go into our New York City or San Francisco office spaces</li> </ul> <p><em>Not sure if you meet the Qualifications? title: Global Procurement Category Lead Engineering and Construction
jd_text: This role leads multiple global Category Management teams and is responsible for overseeing the development and execution of category management strategies across the entire CSL group to ensure best possible value for CSL while managing risk and maintaining compliance in procurement practices. This will be directly involved in major local to global sourcing or bid activities, driving key transformational projects, and building and maintaining relationships with key senior stakeholders internal to CSL Group and within large, global vendors. Responsibilities: Develop Plans aligned to CSL Global and Procurement Strategy Develop and implement global category strategies for both the categories in scope in alignment with corporate strategy and other relevant business strategies within CSL to ensure clear objectives and action plans for Global Category Management Lead roles resulting in the reduction of the total cost of ownership and risk, while increasing innovation, customer service, compliance, and quality. Take a leadership position and drive collaborate with the respective business unit on complex problem resolution, investigative data analytics, process reengineering and establishment of a sustainable program that will fill a global need while being consistent within all Company areas affected. Lead and manage key projects that involve redesign of global strategy, business models and overall ways of working. Drive year over year financial improvements while ensuring operational excellence. Establish and Maintain Effective Category Management and Bid Management Drive value from the global category(s) by defining and implementing effective category management strategies; establishing and managing Councils for business-critical commodities aligned with the evolving business requirements and are effectively leading key sourcing activities, including negotiations, that to deliver lower cost of ownership, lower risk, higher quality, and better supply performance. Lead complex and business negotiations with major key suppliers and provide advice for regional sourcing as required. Conduct business with integrity, in accordance with the highest ethical standards and in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations and anti-bribery requirements and supports diversity and inclusion by promoting utilization of small, disadvantaged and/or diverse suppliers. Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) Establish and manage SRM processes with suppliers within the category as per supplier segmentation, including risk management strategies in accordance with global policies, to enhance relationships and innovations with suppliers to deliver required supply, quality, service, continuous improvement, and innovation while minimizing costs for CSL and develop processes to measure value beyond savings in line with CSL’s values and Procurement strategy. Implement Global procedures to ensure execution of sourcing activities in compliance with CSL Sourcing Policy, Code of Responsible Business Practices, and all other compliance standards. Strictly adhere to the CSL Supplier Risk Management policies and procedures. Utilize the CSL Supplier Risk Management tools as appropriate. Supply Performance Management, including management of Key Performance Indicators Responsible for monitoring Supply Performance KPIs and conducting regular Operational Reviews as per Procurement’s Governance processes with supporting analysis and reporting from the Centre of Excellence and ensuring any Category Management roles within the team also review and manage Supplier performance to meet agreed standards. Develop Talent Lead, motivate and develop employees within the Procurement organization including effective long-term talent development, succession planning and performance managing with a focus on supporting employees to meet or exceed performance expectations while demonstrating CSL Values. Manage Key Internal and External Stakeholders and Partners Relationships Build and maintain effective professional relationships with senior, internal stakeholders and senior external executives within large vendors to deliver upon Procurement’s objectives by ongoing discussions and participation in formal teams and groups with senior leaders in CSL and external vendors to manage supplier performance, issues, procurement improvement initiatives and other broader business issues. Drive Innovation Lead and participate in global transformation projects and continuous improvement initiatives as required to ensure the delivery of targeted benefits. JOB SPECIFICATIONS: Education Master’s degree in Engineering preferred Post graduate business degree, MBA highly regarded Experience Minimum 12 years’ experience in strategic sourcing, other relevant experience in sourcing, or equivalent experience in engineering and construction management. Minimum 2 years senior leadership experience, preferably of a global team. Minimum 5 years in global team management. Strong communication and influencing skills and ability to deal with ambiguity and building bridges Strong understanding of the A&E/EPC/EPCM, CQV/CSV categories and business Understanding of the pharmaceutical industry or related industry preferred but not essential Competencies Maintains an external and strategic focus for self and team Ensures teams are set up for collaboration Creates an accountable working environment Instills personal flexibility in self and team Ensures clarity around the strategy Coaches effectively Additionally, this role requires other knowledge, skills and competencies including: Basic strategic orientation, inquisitive, comfortable with ambiguity, and self-motivated to identify trends and improvement opportunities aligned with business objectives and strategic plans. Strong executive presence demonstrated leadership and collaboration skills with ability to build effective relationships and influence peers and key stakeholders. Demonstrated strength and ability to organize and lead global teams. Strong project management skills with ability to plan tasks, assign resources, manage progress, remove barriers, manage change, resolve conflict, build consensus, and motivate team members across multiple projects concurrently. Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to tailor messages to the given audience, present information in a clear and concise manner, apply creative approaches to engage audiences, manage change, resolve conflict, and build consensus. Solid Category Management, Strategic Sourcing, and Supplier Relationship Management knowledge The position also requires the ability to build and maintain strong relationships and collaborate effectively with all levels and cross functionally within the organization. Travel Requirements Domestic travel as required (10-30%) International travel as required (10-20%) Travel requirements will vary depending upon where the incumbent is based. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives. title: Fixed Income Operations Analyst

We have become a multibillion-dollar asset manager, and we have ambitious goals for the future. Your colleagues will include internationally recognized experts in machine learning research as well as highly experienced finance and technology professionals. Our firm and its strategies are the product of many years of meticulous research and craftsmanship, and you will lead the way in bringing them to investors. In addition to our enriching and collegial working environment, we offer highly competitive compensation and benefits packages, technology talks by our experts, a beautiful modern office, daily catered lunches, and more. This role sits within the Fund Operations team, working closely with colleagues across trading, research, and accounting. You will report directly to the Fund Operations Manager and collaborate regularly with senior leadership, including the CFO. This position offers a unique opportunity to make a tangible impact as a core member of Voleon’s credit operations function. RESPONSIBILITIES - Oversee fixed income trade settlement operations, including trade exception management, inquiries, allocations, fail resolution, and position transfers - Manage the end-to-end corporate actions process by conducting research, evaluating event details, and coordinating with traders on elections and potential liabilities - Maintain and summarize an internal workboard leveraged by trading, research, and engineering teams, ensuring effective communication and cross-functional alignment - Reconcile internal books and records with the prime brokers and fund administrator, promptly investigating and resolving breaks - Collaborate with the Fund Accounting team to ensure all transactions are accurately recorded, including participation in cash reconciliations and month-end reviews - Enhance operational efficiency through process improvements and automation initiatives - Support firm-wide projects such as broker onboardings, restructurings, and new account setups - Participate in cross-training programs, workflow reviews, and coverage planning to promote team scalability and resilience - Liaise with external service providers to identify process improvements and maintain compliance with evolving policies and control standards - Contribute to the development and refinement of internal policies, procedures, and best practices REQUIREMENTS - 5-10 years of finance experience, ideally in an operations role or other middle office role at a hedge fund, broker-dealer, or fund administrator - Ability to work between the hours of 7am to 5pm PST - Advanced abilities in Microsoft Excel - Experience working with or the ability to learn enterprise-level accounting software and develop efficient processes - Experience automating manual processes (preferred) with a focus on leveraging AI LLMs and AI coding tools - Experience working for a hedge fund, broker-dealer, or fund administrator and simple accounting for monthly-close (preferred) - Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Economics, or Accounting (preferred) - Deep knowledge of power infrastructure including utility interconnection, grid capacity analysis, and substation development - Familiarity with permitting processes, environmental review, and land use entitlements for large-scale industrial facilities - Experience working with utility companies, municipalities, and economic development agencies - Ability to build and present complex financial models and location analyses to senior leadership - Willingness to travel frequently to evaluate sites and engage local stakeholders Preferred Qualifications - title: Advisor - Grid Interconnection
jd_text: At ERCOT, our diverse and dynamic work environment provides a platform on which employees can work together to build the future of the Texas power grid and wholesale market utilizing the latest technologies and resources. We encourage you to join our talented, dedicated workforce to develop world-class solutions for today and tomorrow’s energy challenges while learning new skills and growing your career. ERCOT is committed to fostering inclusion at all levels of our company. It is the cornerstone of our corporate values of accountability, leadership, innovation, trust, and expertise. We know that individuals with a wide variety of talents, ideas, and experiences propel the innovation that drives our success. An inclusive and diverse workforce strengthens us and allows for a collaborative environment to solve the challenges that face our industry today and in the future. Creates and communicates a vision that anticipates, identifies, and explains challenges and opportunities in ERCOT’s grid interconnection, including Large Load interconnection. Develops approaches, processes, and engineering solutions that increase ERCOT’s capabilities in evaluating system performance, integrating emerging technologies, and ensuring system reliability. Exerts enterprise-wide technical influence through advanced problem-solving and subject matter expertise. JOB DUTIES Recognized as a subject matter expert with advanced technical skills and competencies; frequently contributes to the development of new theories and methods. Employs highly developed problem-resolution skills using professional concepts and ERCOT objectives to resolve complex issues. Exercises significant latitude in determining objectives, methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for assignments. Advises and leads work of lower-level engineers and provides program/project leadership within matrixed teams. Interacts with management and senior customers on matters requiring coordination across organizational boundaries. Develops methodologies, criteria, and modeling expectations for evaluating Generation Resource and Large Load interconnections, including modeling requirements for synchronous machines, inverter-based resources, and large industrial loads. Leads the technical development of new processes to enable the interconnection of large flexible loads and large loads co-located with new generation. Develops and proposes new rules, guidelines, study practices, and modeling requirements for emerging technologies—including battery energy storage systems, hybrid resources, distributed generation, and large flexible loads—and supports Protocol and Guide Revision Requests through the ERCOT stakeholder process. Represents ERCOT in external technical forums, conferences, NERC groups, IEEE working groups, and ISO/RTO collaboration efforts by providing expertise on interconnection practices, system performance, stability criteria, and emerging technology impacts. Publishes conceptual papers, study methodology documents, and technical reports that advance industry understanding of interconnection studies, system analysis techniques, and modeling of emerging technologies. Mentors ERCOT engineers in advanced interconnection analysis techniques and provides coaching on interpretation of complex technical results and the development of high-quality engineering reports. Provides technical guidance to leadership on complex interconnection and system analysis issues, including evaluation of reliability risks, operational impacts, and long-term implications of new technologies or system trends. Provides technical guidance to leadership on the uses of AI for improving Interconnection processes. Performs other duties as assigned. REQUIRED EXPERIENCE Requires minimum 10 years of job-related experience in Wholesale-Electric Systems Operations, Transmission Planning, System Operations, Grid Operations, Interconnection Studies, or Power System Modeling required Prior experience supervising or leading a team or project required Experience performing interconnection evaluation event analysis, and dynamic models is preferred PREFERRED EXPERIENCE Experience with the ERCOT stakeholder process Experience with stability analysis Experience presenting at industry conferences Participation in industry groups such as NERC, IEEE, etc. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Demonstrate rigorous intellectual ability to articulate complex technical concepts and challenge conventional thinking in their area of expertise and across organizational lines Demonstrate ability to work independently, participate on a team, lead a team, or mentor ERCOT staff with responsibilities that require the highest levels of technical expertise, initiative and resourcefulness Demonstrate highly advanced achievement in their field of expertise by developing approaches, processes and solutions that allow ERCOT to maximize its effectiveness or achieve strategic or operational goals Make a material contribution to expansion of ERCOT’s capabilities and innovation in the fields of science, technology, engineering or mathematics Interacts with management and senior staff on matters requiring coordination across organizational lines. May provide input into organization policy within area of their expertise. Demonstrate ability to lead by influence and build consensus amongst staff in controversial work matters Be recognized by their co-workers, and professional peers as a regional or industry-wide authority in their area of expertise, as evidenced by any of the following: 1. participating in regional or national advisory boards, panels or committees in their field of expertise 2. delivering presentations and addresses pertaining to their area of expertise at industry or professional events 3. teaching certificate-level or college-level courses pertaining to their area of expertise 4. publishing original works of authorship pertaining to their field of expertise in reputable professional or academic publications or journals EDUCATION Bachelor’s Degree: Electrical Engineering or related field (Required) Master’s Degree: Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, or related field (Preferred) or a combination of education and experience that provides equivalent knowledge to a major in such fields is required CERTIFICATION PE – Professional Engineer (Preferred) WORK LOCATION – Taylor, TX: Employees will be required to be on-site in Taylor, TX at a minimum of 2 days per week, or more, as needed based on the business needs as determined by management Remote work is required to be performed from your Texas residence. title: Team Lead Operations Account Management
jd_text: The Team Lead, Operations Account Management is responsible for day‑to‑day operational performance and execution for assigned clients, serving as the primary operations liaison between client facilities and internal delivery teams. This role focuses on tactical revenue cycle outcomes, ensuring accurate reporting, effective communication, and consistent execution across billing, follow‑up, collections, denials, and claim resolution workflows. This position is accountable for operational monitoring and client relationship management. The Team Lead translates client needs into clear operational priorities, monitors key performance indicators, identifies risks and trends, and supports timely issue resolution to protect cash, A/R performance, and client satisfaction. The role also provides operational mentorship to staff by reinforcing daily best practices, supporting training and performance efforts, and helping remove execution barriers. Success is measured by client retention, escalation volume, and core revenue cycle performance indicators. These Goals and objectives are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed; employees will be required to perform other job-related duties as required. Goals and objectives are subject to change. All activities must be in compliance with Equal Employment Opportunity laws, HIPAA, ERISA and other regulations, as appropriate. Essential Functions: In addition to meeting performance expectations, this role includes the following specific responsibilities: Discrete Responsibilities (Primary Accountability) Operational Performance Monitoring: Monitor daily operational performance, battle cards, action plans, and key KPIs for assigned clients, including A/R days, cash performance, denial trends, and accuracy measures. Primary Operations Liaison: Act as the primary operational point of contact between clients and internal delivery teams, ensuring timely, accurate, and consistent communication. Operational Translation: Translate client needs, issues, and requests into actionable operational priorities and execution plans. Risk & Trend Identification: Identify operational risks, analyze performance trends, and support issue resolution to prevent revenue leakage and service disruption. Reporting & Communication: Ensure accurate reporting, clear status updates, and effective issue communication to internal stakeholders and, as appropriate, client contacts. Client Scope: Lead operational work for domestic‑only clients as needed. Reporting, Trend Monitoring & Continuous Improvement Trend Monitoring & Corrective Action: Review statistical reports and dashboards to identify operational trends, risks, and deficiencies; develop and implement corrective action plans to improve timeliness, quality, and outcomes. Operational Efficiency: Lead tactical efforts to maximize operational efficiency and optimize reimbursement through standardized workflows, issue triage, and collaboration with cross-functional partners. Client & Stakeholder Relationship Management (Tactical) Liaison & Communication: Act as the primary operational point of contact between facility management and internal teams, ensuring smooth, timely communication and resolution of day-to-day issues. Service Responsiveness & Escalation: Ensure client inquiries are addressed promptly (including providing timelines to resolution), and proactively escalate risks such as unbilled accounts, claim issues, and operational blockers to leadership. Cross-Functional Coordination: Partner with internal teams (e.g., operations, finance, payer relations, technology, and strategic client management/sales counterparts) to drive resolution and maintain a consistent client experience. Contract Awareness & Compliance: Understand contract terms and ensure operational billing, invoicing, and service delivery remain within negotiated requirements. Compliance & Professional Standards Regulatory Knowledge: Maintain current knowledge of hospital billing systems, government payer programs, third-party reimbursement policies, and applicable federal/state regulations. Confidentiality: Maintain confidentiality of patient and client information without exception. Continuous Learning & Industry Awareness: Attend required meetings and remain current on industry trends, legislative changes, and best practices. Customer Invoicing & Accuracy: Ensure accuracy of customer invoices and support monthly invoicing processes as required; validate supporting detail and address discrepancies. Management Expectations / Additional Duties: Perform all functions in alignment with management expectations and complete other duties as assigned. Key Measures of Success Client Retention and Stability Reduction in Client Escalations Cash Performance vs. Goal A/R Days and Denial Trends Staff Management Responsible for ensuring area of responsibility has the talent and resources to meet short- and long-term organizational goals as well as ensuring maximum productivity and performance. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Proactively recruit, screen, and select candidates for current and future resource requirements. Effectively orient new hires to ensure a positive and productive employee engagement experience. Ensure structure and hiring plans (within budget) are appropriate for performance and productivity levels required. Utilize the company’s performance management program as designed to align individual performance to overall performance objectives. Meet all completion requirements at a high quality level. Provide ongoing performance feedback. Identify and take appropriate action for non-performance. Ensure each employee has a yearly performance review that is reviewed with employee and the review to be sent to Human Resources each year. Ensure each employee has a clear and thorough understanding of their role and responsibilities. Keep job descriptions current for each position. Actively support and participate in organizational development and training programs. Meet all completion requirements at a high quality level. Mentor, guide, and coach direct reports in order to expand their capabilities and performance. Communicate all corporate matters in a positive and timely manner as directed by Corporate Communications or senior managements. Administer all internal policies and procedures in accordance with corporate, human resources, budgetary, and finance guidelines. Ensure accuracy of staff data records. Comply with all employment laws and regulations including, but not limited to, equal employment opportunities for all. Minimum Requirements: Education/Experience/Certification Requirements Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience (to support internal flexibility for hiring and promotion). 5+ years of experience in hospital revenue cycle functions with strong exposure to billing and follow-up/collections and claim resolution. Working knowledge of insurance regulations, reimbursement practices, procedure and diagnosis coding, and automated billing workflows. Demonstrated ability to work issues to resolution, including complex account research, root cause identification, and corrective actions. Strong client-facing communication skills (written and verbal) with the ability to explain operational findings, timelines, and next steps clearly. Excellent critical thinking, organizational, and time-management skills with strong attention to detail, accuracy, and follow-through. Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Outlook, Word) and comfort working across multiple systems and reporting outputs. Preferred Qualifications: 2+ years Medicare hospital billing experience and/or demonstrated expertise with government payers (Medicare/Medicaid). Experience supporting hospital billing platforms and/or EHR/RCM systems (e.g., Thrive, Epic, Cerner, or comparable tools). Advanced revenue cycle analytics capability (e.g., trending denials/underpayments, operational KPI reporting, dashboard interpretation). Prior experience in a role requiring client management, escalations, service recovery, and cross-functional coordination. Exposure to invoicing processes, contract compliance validation, and operational performance governance. Manager

title: Pharmacy Technician
jd_text: We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time. Position Summary Health is everything. At CVS Health, we are committed to increasing patient access to care, lowering costs and improving the quality of care. Millions of times a day, we’re helping people on their path to better health— from advising patients on their prescriptions to helping them manage their chronic and specialty conditions. Because we’re present in so many moments, big and small, we have an active, supportive role in shaping the future of health care. Pharmacy Technicians are at the forefront of our purpose as they deliver compassionate care to our millions of patients every day. Come join our team of dedicated and caring Pharmacy Technicians who demonstrate our core values of Accountability, Caring, Collaboration,Innovation and Integrity in everything they do in our pharmacies every day. Whether you are new to working in pharmacies or are an experienced Pharmacy Technician, we have a place for you on our team to use your skills and talents to serve and care for our patients and customers. The Pharmacy Technician position provides individuals with an opportunity to work in a leading retail pharmacy company and in a role that positively impacts the lives and health of others. You will work in an environment where the highest professional and ethical standards are maintained as well as full compliance with all Federal, State and Local laws and regulations. Pharmacy Technicians take important steps to ensure all medication needs and regulatory compliance standards are met for our patients and they demonstrate ethical conduct and maintain patient confidentiality at all times. Success for incumbents in this role includes being able to manage all assigned pharmacy workstations and tasks to support the team’s ability to promptly, safely and accurately fill patient prescriptions all while providing caring service that exceeds customer expectations. If you like working in fast-paced environments and demonstrating compassionate, genuine care for patients and customers, this job is for you! As a new Pharmacy Technician, you are required to complete an extensive CVS Pharmacy Technician Training Program as well as satisfy all registration, licensing and certification requirements according to your State’s Board of Pharmacy guidelines. Your Pharmacy Technician duties will be restricted by your manager at first until you complete all necessary requirements. Once you satisfy all requirements and expand your Pharmacy Technician duties, you have the opportunity to continue to build your clinical, technical and insurance knowledge and expertise by leveraging available tools and training to build your pharmacy career. Are you ready to help people on their path to better health? We are ready to have you join our team and help you on your career path to achieve your goals! Please note in select markets the collective bargaining agreement rules regarding the Pharmacy Technician would apply. title: Vice President, AI Architect (Remote)
jd_text: As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you. About the Role: We’re looking for a VP-level AI Architect to define and drive a consistent, modern AI- and agentic-first architecture across CrowdStrike. This company-wide role spans business units, customer-facing products, shared platforms, and internal AI capabilities. You’ll connect AI applications with the software and infrastructure that make them work at scale. Working with business unit and engineering leaders, you’ll translate business priorities into practical designs, establish common technical foundations, and guide implementation across teams. The architecture must support distinct product needs while making shared capabilities easier to build, integrate, and operate. Your work will range from company-wide architectural decisions to building reference implementations and resolving difficult engineering problems. You’ll bring deep systems expertise, sound judgment about emerging AI technologies, and a record of turning architectural direction into working products. What You’ll Do: Define and drive the company-wide AI architecture and roadmap. Establish shared interfaces and design patterns, resolve cross-business-unit tradeoffs, and work with product and engineering leaders to put architectural decisions into practice. Determine which capabilities should be common and where teams need flexibility. Design and build full-stack AI and agentic systems. Connect models and retrieval to agent runtimes, memory, tools, and execution environments. Develop prototypes and production reference implementations that give teams a tested foundation for new capabilities. Architect production AI systems for performance, resilience, and scale. Benchmark model and serving options, investigate bottlenecks across software and infrastructure, and improve latency, throughput, and compute efficiency. Guide deployment choices across cloud and edge environments. Create a consistent developer experience across products through reusable components, common APIs, and shared tooling. Simplify integration and establish engineering practices that teams adopt. Contribute to critical implementations, review designs and code, and mentor engineers and technical leaders. Design the AI lifecycle architecture, from data ingestion and model adaptation through evaluation, deployment, and operational feedback. Establish reproducible workflows, automated quality gates, and observability for model quality, agent task success, reliability, and cost. Build safe rollout, rollback, and recovery into production systems. Embed security, governance, and auditability into AI architectures. Define permissions and execution boundaries for agents, address prompt injection and data exposure, and make system actions traceable. Partner with Security and Legal to translate requirements into practical engineering controls. What You’ll Need: BS, MS, or PhD in computer science, computer engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 10+ years of experience in software architecture, systems engineering, or AI engineering, including senior technical leadership across multiple products or business units. A record of personally designing and delivering production AI systems, including generative or agentic applications and the infrastructure that supports them. Strong foundations in distributed systems, software design, APIs, and performance engineering, with the ability to work across application and infrastructure layers. Practical experience with model integration, inference serving, retrieval, and evaluation, including the tradeoffs involved in deploying and operating AI systems at scale. Experience establishing shared platforms and engineering standards across independent teams. Ability to align senior stakeholders, explain architectural tradeoffs, and mentor engineers through implementation. Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes. Bonus Points: Significant contributions to open-source projects or industry standards, with experience shaping technical direction across external engineering communities and partners. Depth in Linux systems software, networking, accelerated computing, or AI deployment across cloud and edge environments. Experience modernizing established platforms into AI-native systems, particularly in cybersecurity or other environments with demanding security and reliability requirements. title: Compliance Analyst Sr - Operations and Planning
jd_text: At ERCOT, our diverse and dynamic work environment provides a platform on which employees can work together to build the future of the Texas power grid and wholesale market utilizing the latest technologies and resources. We encourage you to join our talented, dedicated workforce to develop world-class solutions for today and tomorrow’s energy challenges while learning new skills and growing your career. ERCOT is committed to fostering inclusion at all levels of our company. It is the cornerstone of our corporate values of accountability, leadership, innovation, trust, and expertise. We know that individuals with a wide variety of talents, ideas, and experiences propel the innovation that drives our success. An inclusive and diverse workforce strengthens us and allows for a collaborative environment to solve the challenges that face our industry today and in the future. JOB SUMMARY The Operations and Planning (O&P) Compliance role supports ERCOT's adherence to NERC Operations and Planning Reliability Standards and ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Operating Guides, and Other Binding Documents. The position collaborates with internal teams within the organization to identify and assess internal controls, consider compliance risks, and conduct remediation to ensure compliance with Federal Energy Regulatory Commission orders, North American Reliability Corporation Reliability (NERC) Standards, Regional Reliability Standards, ERCOT Nodal Protocols and Operating Guides, and corporate objectives (“requirements”). This role works closely with ERCOT personnel to identify the documentation and other controls related to the various requirements and ensures policies and procedures are in place to demonstrate compliance with requirements. This position acts as the primary liaison between the organization’s staff, regulatory agencies, and external auditors. JOB DUTIES Level 2 Applies analytical and problem-solving skills to independently identify compliance risks and develop effective solutions. Uses compliance methods and tools to monitor and report on compliance with requirements, with moderate independence. Acts as a resource to advise process owners on improving processes and compliance posture. Works with assigned groups to develop, implement, and manage routine operations reports relevant to documenting and demonstrating performance compliance to requirements. Assists business process owners with oversight of remediation of issues resulting from internal and external audits, compliance investigations, and control assessments. Prepares ERCOT staff and documentation for NERC, Texas RE, and other external audits; maintains documentation of business processes and related internal controls; participates in audits as needed. Develops and maintains analytical documentation comparing current and revised NERC Operations and Planning Reliability Standards, ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Operating Guides, OBDs, and ERCOT policies; aligns obligations with internal controls, including business processes and procedures. Prepares and maintains NERC Reliability Standard Audit Worksheets (RSAWs), narratives, evidence, and internal controls for assigned Standards, coordinating with subject matter experts. Uses the Archer GRC platform to monitor, review, and assess the design and operational effectiveness of internal controls mapped to Reliability Standards and ERCOT Nodal Protocols requirements. Supports ERCOT's representation with NERC and Regional Standards Committees through participation on drafting teams or submission to development efforts. Develops or monitors recommendations providing guidance on NERC standards and ERCOT Regional Reliability standards directly impacting ERCOT systems, capabilities, and reliability. Participates in activities of developing or revising NERC Operations and Planning Reliability Standards, ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Operating Guides, and OBD provisions with ERCOT committees as applicable. Supports performance and Ancillary Services monitoring under ERCOT Nodal Protocols Section 8 and Nodal Operating Guides Section 9, including reporting to the Reliability Monitor. Level Senior Coordinates and communicates on NERC Operations and Planning Reliability Standards, ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Operating Guides, and OBDs provisions with ERCOT committees and Board of Directors as needed. Develops and manages the process to collect and submit ERCOT feedback on NERC Operations and Planning Standards postings. Evaluates and maintains the relevance of traces from ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Operating Guides, OBDs, NERC Operations and Planning Reliability Standards, and corporate objectives to other ERCOT documentation. Facilitates the development of internal training regarding external audits and associated business processes and controls. Assists with coordination of external audits, including acting as a primary liaison between ERCOT staff and the auditors Updates compliance tools, tracks effort and progress of audits and investigations, and manages library of audit documentation Communicates technical compliance information effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences and works effectively across cross-functional teams. Documents and tracks potential compliance issues (self-logs and self-reports) and responds to Requests for Information (RFIs) from regulators. EXPERIENCE Level 2: Requires 2 years related work experience Level Senior: Require 5 years related work experience Prefer experience with NERC Operations and Planning Reliability Standards and the ERCOT Nodal Protocols, Operating Guides, and OBDs. Prefer experience with Bulk Electric System (BES) operations and/or planning, NERC compliance monitoring, RSAW and evidence development, and Texas Reliability Entity and/or NERC audits. Prefer experience with SQL, Cognos, Python, or other data analysis platforms EDUCATION Bachelor's Degree: Engineering, Computer Science, Business, Accounting, Auditing or related field (Required) or a combination of education and experience that provides equivalent knowledge to a major in such fields is required CERTIFICATION CCEP Certified Compliance Ethics Professional (Preferred) NERC System Operator Certification (Preferred) The foregoing description reflects the minimum qualifications and the essential functions of the position that must be performed proficiently with or without reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities. It is not an exhaustive list of the duties expected to be performed, and management may, at its discretion, revise or require that other or different tasks be performed as assigned. title: Planning Engineer Lead - Dynamic Studies
jd_text: At ERCOT, our diverse and dynamic work environment provides a platform on which employees can work together to build the future of the Texas power grid and wholesale market utilizing the latest technologies and resources. JOB SUMMARY Provides comprehensive electrical engineering analysis and technical support for Large Load Batch stability assessment, NERC reliability studies, transmission planning, and interconnection reliability assessments pertaining to Large Loads integration within the ERCOT power system. Utilizes robust system modeling techniques, study tools and procedures for evaluating system performance, conducts stability analyses, formulates solutions to address system reliability requirements, and presents findings and recommendations in a clear and appropriate manner. Level 3: Performs Batch stability screening studies for Large Load interconnection and transmission improvements using power system simulation tools. Designs and performs stability assessments, including but not limited to PV analysis, angular and voltage stability, and short circuit analysis, using simulation models (PSSE, VSAT, TSAT, PowerWorld, and/or related tools) under the direction of a senior engineer or management. Supports NERC FAC-002 studies for Large Load interconnections. Runs appropriate scenarios and sensitivity analyses to ensure robust study results, analyzes study accuracy, and assists in formulating conclusions and recommendations. Reviews stakeholder reports and dynamic models to ensure appropriate technical content and accuracy. Identifies stability constraints and assists in developing mitigation recommendations. Assists in preparing technical reports, presentations, and study documentation for ERCOT management, Market Participants, NERC, and other entities. Supports process improvements and automation efforts for planning and stability screening workflows. Assists market participants in updating and validating power system dynamic models. Ability to manage multiple assignments and competing priorities. Commitment to reliability, compliance, technical accuracy, and continuous improvement. Senior Level: includes all of the above in addition to: Serves as a technical Subject Matter Expert for Batch Zero stability screening. Makes independent decisions except in instances of unusually complex engineering scenarios. Works on the most complex engineering issues where analysis of situations requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors. Has the ability to resolve complex issues in creative and effective ways. Leads complex interconnection and reliability studies involving resources, Large Loads, and transmission system improvements. May coordinate, provide presentations, and participate in stakeholder meetings with ERCOT personnel, Market Participants, Transmission Service Providers, consultants, and Regulatory agencies. Fosters and leverages strong working relationships with team members and other internal departments. Leads professional expertise to guide projects and help teammates assigned by management. Acts as mentor and advisor to less experienced engineers/analysts. Leads multifunctional teams to obtain input, address comments, and perform studies. Demonstrates skills as an expert user of power system software applications and tools. Maintains knowledge of emerging trends and industry best practices related to system stability, interconnection studies, and reliability standards. Excellent written and verbal communication abilities. Lead Level: includes all of the above in addition to: Broadly applies advanced engineering principles, theories, and concepts with full-depth expertise in transmission planning, stability analysis, and interconnection studies. Independently defines problem statements, study scope, and analytical approaches for complex, ambiguous issues where established procedures may not exist. Leads and delivers highly complex stability studies of diverse scope, exercising sound judgment in selecting methods, assumptions, and solution strategies. Provides technical recommendations on issues that extend beyond standard practices, influencing project, program, or departmental outcomes. Serves as a recognized technical authority and primary point of contact, frequently engaging with Market Participants, TSPs, consultants, and external stakeholders. Operates with wide latitude in decision-making within assigned programs and projects; work is reviewed primarily for alignment with objectives and outcomes. Works independently with minimal supervision; receives general direction on new or strategic assignments. Acts as a lead engineer and resource to senior and junior staff, guiding, reviewing, and at times directing technical work. Represents the organization in project leadership roles and high-impact stakeholder or inter-organizational forums. REQUIREMENTS Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or related field required Or a combination of education and experience that provides equivalent knowledge equivalent to a major in such fields is required. Work Experience Required Engineer 3 – Requires a minimum of 3 years job-related work experience (in excess of degree requirements stated above) as a power system engineer or similar type role. Experience within the electric utility industry preferred. Engineer, Sr. – Requires a minimum of 5 years job-related work experience (in excess of degree requirements stated above) of experience as a power system engineer or similar type role. Experience within the electric utility industry preferred. Lead – Requires a minimum 8 years job-related experience (in excess of degree requirements stated above) of experience as a power system engineer or similar type role. Experience within the electric utility industry preferred. Preferred Work Experience: Experience performing stability studies. Experience supporting transmission planning assessments. Experience conducting large-scale dynamic stability analyses using power system simulation tools Experience analyzing large load dynamic behavior (e.g., data centers, industrial loads) and assessing system impacts. Experience programming and developing simulation automation tools (Python preferred). Experience assessing and mitigating oscillatory or voltage stability issues. Experience assisting in the development of improvements to transmission planning and interconnection study processes. Familiarity with NERC reliability standards, particularly FAC-002 and TPL standards. WORK LOCATION This position is Hybrid. Employees will be required to be on-site in Taylor, TX at least 2–3 days per week, or more, as needed based on the business needs as determined by management. Remote work is required to be performed from your Texas residence. Employees may opt to work on-site more than required or 100% of the time. JOB SUMMARY Manages ERCOT Release Engineering Services function encompassing three core delivery disciplines — Release DevOps Engineering (CI/CD, automated deployments, DevSecOps, and pipeline operations), Release Planning and Governance (product release planning, backlog facilitation, change management, and ITSM governance), and Release and Scope Management (release scope baselining, formal scope change control, and traceability from approved backlog items through production deployment). Leads a team of Release Engineers and Release Train Engineers across all technology stacks and product lines. Responsible for the end-to-end software delivery lifecycle from code commit to production — ensuring releases are automated, scope-controlled, compliant with NERC CIP requirements, governed through ServiceNow, and continuously improved through DORA metrics and retrospective practices. Operates at the intersection of DevOps execution, Agile delivery governance, scope/change control, and regulated change management serving ERCOT's mission to reliably operate the Texas power grid. ADDITIONAL JOB DUTIES Release Engineering Strategy & Toolchain Governance Define and govern the CI/CD pipeline architecture, branching strategy, and deployment toolchain standards (GitHub Actions, Harness, Jenkins, Azure DevOps) across all product lines; ensure engineering practices align to DevOps industry benchmarks and NERC CIP compliance requirements. Production Deployment Oversight Provide management oversight of all deployments to test, UAT, staging, and production environments; govern release readiness criteria, change authorization processes, and rollback decision authority for high-impact releases across Agile and waterfall delivery tracks. Release and Scope Management Own end-to-end release and scope governance for all product lines, ensuring every release is delivered against a formally approved, traceable scope baseline and that scope changes are controlled rather than absorbed informally. Define and baseline release scope for each release cycle and Program Increment, including scope statement, work breakdown of committed backlog items, and acceptance criteria, in alignment with PMI Scope Management practices (Plan Scope, Define Scope, Create WBS, Validate Scope, Control Scope). Establish and enforce scope-lock checkpoints within Agile Release Train (R-train) cadences; require documented justification, impact assessment, and CAB or Release Train Engineer approval for any story, RFC, or requirement introduced after scope lock. Own formal scope change control: evaluate scope change requests against schedule, capacity, risk, and downstream dependencies, and route approved changes through the Change Advisory Board before they enter a committed release. Define and report scope health metrics — stories added after scope lock, silent scope drops, scope creep rate, and stories committed versus delivered per cycle — and integrate them into DORA and executive release reporting. Maintain requirements traceability between the approved scope baseline and shipped deliverables, ensuring RFCs, user stories, and acceptance evidence map back to in-scope items and that out-of-scope requests are logged for future cycles rather than dropped without record. Facilitate scope trade-off and re-prioritization decisions during PI Planning Adjustments, Inspect & Adapt sessions, and mid-cycle re-baselining; balance business demand against team capacity, schedule, and release risk. Serve as the management escalation point for scope disputes between product, engineering, and business stakeholders, ensuring scope decisions are documented, communicated to all teams, and reflected in the release calendar and CAB record. DevSecOps & NERC CIP Compliance Leadership Own the DevSecOps framework for Release Engineering; ensure NERC CIP-aligned controls (vulnerability scanning, SBOM, image signing, secrets management, audit trails) are embedded in all CI/CD pipelines and production deployment workflows. ​ DORA Metrics Governance Own DORA metrics instrumentation and executive reporting for Release Engineering; track deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, and MTTR; drive continuous improvement against DORA elite performance targets. Release Readiness & Production Gate Authority Serve as the management-level gate authority for production releases; validate release readiness criteria, scope completion against the approved baseline, test completion evidence, and all stakeholder approvals before deployment execution. Own IT change metric definitions and executive reporting; track change volume by type, change success rate, unauthorized change incidents, CAB throughput, and change-to-incident correlation via ServiceNow and Power BI. Serve as the primary management interface between Release Engineering Services, product teams, infrastructure, Cloud Ops, Security, and business leadership; communicate release status, scope, risk, and governance decisions to audiences from team leads to VP level. Lead cross-function retrospectives and Inspect & Adapt sessions spanning Release Engineering, Release Planning, and Release/Scope Management; measure improvement impact using DORA metrics, flow metrics, scope stability metrics, and ITC change success rates. Serve as the management escalation authority for critical production deployment decisions, major pipeline incidents, scope disputes, and emergency change requests. EXPERIENCE Requires minimum 8 years of experience in Release Engineering, DevOps, Platform Engineering, or Release Management, including at least 2 years in a people management or technical leadership role spanning CI/CD pipeline ownership, ITSM change management governance, and release scope management. Requires demonstrated technical depth in CI/CD tooling (GitHub Actions, Harness, Jenkins, or Azure DevOps), DevSecOps practices (NERC CIP or equivalent compliance controls), and ITSM platforms (ServiceNow Change Management). Experience managing both software deployment engineering and release governance functions strongly preferred. Requires experience managing delivery across Agile (Scrum, SAFe, Kanban), waterfall, and hybrid delivery methodologies. Must demonstrate ability to govern DORA metrics programs, lead CAB processes, and drive continuous improvement across cross-functional engineering and planning teams. Requires demonstrated experience governing release and project scope across the full delivery lifecycle, including scope baselining and formal change control (per PMI Scope Management practices: Plan Scope, Define Scope, Create WBS, Validate Scope, Control Scope), scope-lock enforcement within Agile Release Train (SAFe PI) cadences, and requirements traceability from approved backlog items through production deployment. title: Managing Consultant, Safe and Sustainable Operations
jd_text: Lead the transformation of EHS programs from compliance obligations to strategic business advantages. At ERM , we help organizations solve complex environmental, health, and safety challenges while advancing operational excellence and sustainability. In this role, you will manage projects and contribute technically to challenging EHS compliance, management systems, auditing, and compliance assurance projects and programs for clients locally, nationally, and internationally. What Your Impact Is Serve as project manager and deliver EHS compliance and management system projects that reduce risk and strengthen regulatory performance. Serve as a trusted advisor to clients, shaping EHS strategy and driving long-term program success. Elevate EHS programs from compliance-driven to performance-oriented and sustainability-aligned. Build and expand client relationships, generating repeat business and contributing to regional growth. Mentor and develop talent, fostering a high-performing and collaborative team environment. What You'll Bring Required BS in engineering (chemical, mechanical, environmental), environmental science, or related degree, or equivalent experience. 4-6 years (7+ years preferred) of relevant multimedia EHS compliance and management systems, including consulting experience. Strong technical knowledge in EHS compliance areas (e.g., e-waste, hazardous waste, stormwater, wastewater, and/or EPCRA). Experience with assessing regulatory applicability of regulations; compliance reporting; and communicating with and working with regulatory agencies. Experience writing proposals and managing projects, budgets, and timelines with accountability for quality outcomes. Demonstrated ability to lead initiatives, delegate effectively, and mentor team members. Excellent communication, analytical, and stakeholder management skills. Positive outlook and collaborative approach. Ability to travel up to 25%. This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. Preferred MS in engineering (chemical, mechanical, environmental), environmental science, or related degree. Professional certifications (e.g., PE, CSP, CHMM). Experience working with auditing compliance programs, including e-waste, waste, stormwater, wastewater, and/or EPCRA. Experience with developing, maintaining and/or auditing EHS management systems (ISO 14001 / ISO 45001, R2, RIOS, ISO 9001). Key Responsibilities Lead EHS compliance audits, assessments, and corrective action implementation across client operations. Develop and implement EHS management systems and regulatory programs (water, waste, spill prevention). Provide support for permit application development and regulatory agency communication. Provide on-site compliance support and technical expertise at client facilities. Manage multiple projects end-to-end, ensuring delivery within scope, schedule, and budget. Identify and develop new opportunities, prepare effective technical proposals, and take an active leadership role in developing new business with new and existing clients. As a project manager, work closely with clients and ERM teams to achieve client expectations for scope, budget, schedule, and quality. Build and maintain strong client relationships to drive repeat business and new opportunities. Prepare proposals, identify growth opportunities, and contribute to expanding ERM's EHS services. Mentor junior staff, delegate work effectively, and support team development and performance. Collaborate with ERM's global network to share best practices and deliver innovative solutions. title: Generation Interconnection Engineer
jd_text: At ERCOT, our diverse and dynamic work environment provides a platform on which employees can work together to build the future of the Texas power grid and wholesale market utilizing the latest technologies and resources. We encourage you to join our talented, dedicated workforce to develop world-class solutions for today and tomorrow’s energy challenges while learning new skills and growing your career. Engineer 1 · Develops thorough understanding of the entire generation interconnection process from the initial application to the approval for commercial operations. · Under the direction of management and senior engineers, ensures that the interconnection of generation and energy storage resources are accomplished in a manner that maintains the reliability of the ERCOT System and complies with the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Standards, ERCOT Protocols, Planning Guide and the Operating Guides. Works closely with Market Participants (MPs), including Interconnecting Entities (IEs), Resource entities (REs), Distribution Service Providers (DSPs), and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs). · Works closely with ERCOT System Operations, System Operations Support, Market Operating Services Support, Client Services, System Planning and Metering. · Reviews and processes generation interconnection and FIS applications. · Performs security screening studies to determine first contingency incremental transfer capability for each interconnection request. · Attends FIS kickoff meetings, communicates and works with MPs and other ERCOT departments to solve issues related to generation interconnection projects. · May review and approve Reactive Study reports, FIS scope and reports, and Standard Generation Interconnection Agreements. · May review and approve modeling data for planning phase of the interconnection process. Engineer 2 · Able to manage the integration of generation and energy storage resources through the entire generation interconnection process, from the initial application to the approval for commercial operations, without close supervision. · Ensures that the interconnection of generation and energy storage resources are accomplished in a manner that maintains the reliability of the ERCOT System and complies with the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Standards, ERCOT Protocols, Planning Guide and the Operating Guides. Works closely with Market Participants (MPs), including Interconnecting Entities (IEs), Resource entities (REs), Distribution Service Providers (DSPs), and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs). · Works closely with ERCOT System Operations, System Operations Support, Market Operating Services Support, Client Services, System Planning and Metering. · Reviews and processes generation interconnection and FIS applications. · Performs security screening studies to determine first contingency incremental transfer capability for each interconnection request. · Attends FIS kickoff meetings, communicates and works with MPs and other ERCOT departments to solve issues related to generation interconnection projects. · Reviews and approves Reactive Study reports, FIS scope and reports, and Standard Generation Interconnection Agreements. · May provide training and mentorship to Engineer Development Program (EDP) engineers. · May review and approve modeling data for planning phase of the interconnection process. · May review commissioning testing data, including but not limited to AVR/PSS, and Reactive tests. Engineer 3 · Performs all the above duties of an Engineer 2 as well as the following. · Reviews Commissioning Plan and Energization, Synchronization, and Commissioning checklists. · Reviews commissioning testing data, including but not limited to AVR/PSS, and Reactive tests. · Reviews and approves modeling data for planning phase of the interconnection process. · May support Network Modeling to model the generation resource in the Operations model. · May develop and maintain tools that automates the studies, reviews, and other processes. · May provide training to less experienced engineers. · May review, draft, and implement improvements to the interconnection and modeling process. Engineer Sr · Performs all the above duties of an Engineer 3 as well as the following. · Reviews and approves modeling data for all phases of the interconnection process and supports Network Modeling to model the generation resource in the Operations model. · May represent ERCOT at stakeholder meetings as directed by management. · Develops and maintains tools that automates the studies, reviews, and other processes. · Provides training to less experienced engineers. · Reviews, drafts, and implements improvements to the interconnection and modeling process. · May review, draft, and present changes to the Protocols, Guides, procedures, training material for other engineers and for MPs, and other supporting ERCOT documents relative to modeling. · Analyzes data related to the generation interconnection process and provides to management when required · May participate in cross-functional teams as a subject matter expert on topics related to interconnection of generation to the ERCOT system. · Provides training and mentorship to Engineer Development Program (EDP) engineers. Engineer Lead · Performs all the above duties of an Engineer Sr. as well as the following. · Serves as primary subject matter expert in one or more portions of the generation interconnection process. · Participates in cross-functional teams as a subject matter expert on topics related to interconnection of generation to the ERCOT system. · Represents ERCOT at stakeholder meetings as directed by management. · Reviews, drafts, and presents changes to the Protocols, Guides, procedures, training material for other engineers and for MPs, and other supporting ERCOT documents relative to modeling. · May participate in the interview process for new engineers. EXPERIENCE Engineer 1: No minimum work experience required Engineer 2: 1 year relevant work experience required Engineer 3: 3 years relevant work experience required Engineer Sr: 5 years relevant work experience required EDUCATION Bachelor's Degree : Electrical Engineering or related field (Required) or a combination of education and experience that provides equivalent knowledge to a major in such fields is required ERCOT is firmly committed to equal employment for all qualified persons without regard to race, sex, medical condition, religion, age, creed, national origin, citizenship status, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, ancestry, veteran status, genetic information or any other protected category under federal, state or local law.
